en.L: And God said, "Let there be lights in the vault of the heavens to separate between the day and the night, and let them be for signs and for appointed times and for days and years,

decisions.choice: lights: lamps, things that give light
decisions.reason: The word is not "light" itself (verse 3) but a holder or source of light, a lamp; it is used for the lampstand in the tabernacle (Exodus 35:14). The lights do not make the light of day; they carry it and rule over it.

decisions.choice: signs that mark appointed times, days and years
alternatives: signs, seasons, days and years: four separate purposes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins four things with "and". They can be four separate purposes, or "signs" can be the main one and the rest what the signs mark. The second fits the sentence better: the lights are the signs by which people know the appointed times and count the days and the years.

decisions.choice: appointed times: the set times of the year, including the festivals
decisions.reason: The word means a fixed time or an appointed meeting, and it is used for Israel's festivals (Leviticus 23:2, 4). The moon and the sun set the calendar by which those times were kept (Psalm 104:19).

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse (L, B)
decisions.reason: God's command runs on into verse 15. Literal and Balanced keep it as one sentence, so this verse ends with a comma; Readable ends the sentence here.

decisions.choice: lumbreras (L); luces (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is a source of light, a lamp, not light itself (m1). Literal says "lumbreras", the older word for a body that gives light, which keeps the difference from "luz" in verse 3. Balanced and Readable say "luces", the ordinary word. "Luminarias" suggests festive lights, and "astros" names the heavenly bodies and loses the idea of a lamp.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced; passé composé at Readable
decisions.reason: The tense choice for French narrative in Genesis, recorded in 1:1: the passé simple of written narrative at Literal and Balanced ("Dieu dit", "Dieu fit"), the passé composé of spoken French at Readable ("Dieu a dit").

decisions.choice: des luminaires (L); des lumières (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is not "light" itself but a holder of light, a lamp (m1). Literal keeps "luminaires", the French word for a body or source of light; Balanced and Readable say "lumières", as the English says "lights". "Astres" would name the sun, moon and stars as such, which the account avoids (verse 16, m1).

decisions.choice: taa (L); mianga (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means a lamp, a holder of light (m1), the word for the lampstand of the tabernacle. Literal says "taa", lamps, to show this; Balanced and Readable say "mianga", the plural of "mwanga", the ordinary word for lights that shine. "Nuru" is kept for light itself (verse 3).

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in the English, God's command runs on into verse 15 at Literal and Balanced; Readable closes each verse as its own sentence.

decisions.choice: "광명체" (L, B); "빛나는 것들" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word here is not the word for light itself (verse 3) but a word for a lamp, a thing that gives light (meaning decision m1). "광명체" (a body that gives light) keeps the two apart at Literal and Balanced; Readable says it in everyday words.

decisions.choice: luzes
decisions.reason: "Luminares" and "luzeiros", the words of the older Portuguese Bibles, are rare today. "Luzes" is the plain word, as the English says "lights"; it is plural and so stays distinct from "a luz" of verse 3 (m1).

decisions.choice: tempos fixados (L, B); as datas especiais do ano (R)
decisions.reason: "Estações" would suggest the four seasons; the word means the set times of the year, festivals among them (m3). Readable says "as datas especiais do ano", as the English Readable says "the special times of the year".

decisions.choice: "ብርሃን ሰጪዎች" (light-givers) for the lights, at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names things that give light, lamps (meaning decision m1), and the sun and moon are not yet named (verse 16). "ብርሃን ሰጪዎች" says what they do in plain words; "ብርሃናት" is an older plural few readers use, and "መብራቶች" now suggests electric lamps.

decisions.choice: "እንዲህ አለ፦" before the speech at Balanced and Readable, where the speech runs on into the next verse
alternatives: "«...» አለ" after the speech, as elsewhere at these levels
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable usually end with "አለ" after the words spoken (see 1:3). This speech ends in verse 15, so the verb of saying is put first here, to keep each verse's content after its own verse number.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Amharic in this passage: pronouns and verbs for God are written once
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns for God has nothing to change in Amharic (see 1:1).
The Hebrew word means things that give light, lamps (m1). The plural of the word for light keeps the link with 1:3 that the Hebrew has.

decisions.choice: "नियत समय" (L, B); "साल के ख़ास समय" (R)
decisions.reason: The appointed times are the set times of the year, festivals included (meaning decision on appointed times), not the seasons of the weather, which "ऋतुएँ" would suggest.

decisions.choice: "светила"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means things that give light (m1); the sun and the moon are not named. "Светило" is the Russian word for a heavenly body that gives light, and keeps them unnamed as well.

decisions.choice: "призначені часи" for the appointed times
decisions.reason: The word covers the set times of the year, festivals included (meaning decision m3); "призначені часи" keeps that open, and Readable says "особливі пори року".

decisions.choice: "光るもの" (L, B), "明かり" (R) for the lights; "定められた時" (L, B), "祭りなどの特別な季節" (R) for the appointed times
decisions.reason: The word means lamps, things that give light (m1), and the appointed times are the set times of the year, including the festivals (m3). 季節 alone would suggest only the weather seasons.

pt.L: E Deus fez as duas grandes luzes, a luz grande para governar o dia e a luz pequena para governar a noite, e as estrelas.

am.L: እግዚአብሔርም ሁለቱን ታላላቅ ብርሃን ሰጪዎች፣ ታላቁን ብርሃን ሰጪ ቀንን እንዲገዛ፣ ታናሹንም ብርሃን ሰጪ ሌሊትን እንዲገዛ፣ ከዋክብትንም ሠራ።

hi.B: परमेश्वर ने दो बड़ी ज्योतियाँ बनाईं, दिन पर शासन करने के लिए बड़ी, और रात पर शासन करने के लिए छोटी। और उन्होंने तारे भी बनाए।
hi.R: परमेश्वर ने दो बड़ी रोशनियाँ बनाईं: बड़ी रोशनी, यानी सूरज, दिन पर राज करने के लिए, और छोटी रोशनी, यानी चाँद, रात पर राज करने के लिए। उन्होंने तारे भी बनाए।

ru.L: И Бог создал два великих светила: великое светило, чтобы править днём, и малое светило, чтобы править ночью, и звёзды.
ru.B: Бог создал два великих светила: большее, чтобы управлять днём, и меньшее, чтобы управлять ночью. И {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} создал звёзды.
ru.R: Бог сделал два больших светила: одно побольше, солнце, чтобы оно управляло днём, и другое поменьше, луну, чтобы она управляла ночью. Ещё {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} сделал звёзды.

uk.L: І зробив Бог два великі світила: велике світило для панування над днем і мале світило для панування над ніччю, і зорі.
uk.B: Бог зробив два великі світила: більше, щоб панувати над днем, і менше, щоб панувати над ніччю. І {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зробив зорі.
uk.R: Бог зробив два великі світила: більше — сонце, щоб правити днем, і менше — місяць, щоб правити ніччю. Він зробив також зорі.

ja.L: そして神は二つの大きな光るものを造られた。昼を治めるための大きな光るものと、夜を治めるための小さな光るもの、また星を。
ja.B: 神は二つの大きな光るものを造り、大きいほうに昼を治めさせ、小さいほうに夜を治めさせられた。また星も造られた。
ja.R: 神は二つの大きな明かりを造られました。大きいほうの太陽には昼を、小さいほうの月には夜を治めさせられました。また星も造られました。

decisions.choice: the great light and the small light: the sun and the moon, left unnamed
decisions.reason: The account does not use the ordinary words for sun and moon, which were also the names of gods worshiped by Israel's neighbors. They are simply lights that God makes and puts in place, with a task to do. Deuteronomy 4:19 warns Israel not to worship the sun, moon and stars, which God has given to all peoples.

decisions.choice: rule: to govern, to have charge of
decisions.reason: The lights are given rule over day and night: they mark and govern the times. Rule over the living creatures is later given to human beings (verses 26 and 28), with a different verb.

decisions.choice: and the stars: added in passing
decisions.reason: The stars are added at the end, with no task of their own, the briefest mention of anything made in the chapter. Elsewhere God counts and names them (Psalm 147:4; Isaiah 40:26).

decisions.choice: great ... small (L); larger ... smaller (B); bigger ... smaller (R)
decisions.reason: Hebrew has no separate form for comparing two things: "the great light" and "the small light" mean the larger and the smaller of the two. Literal keeps the plain words; Balanced and Readable compare.

decisions.choice: the sun ... the moon
alternatives: the bigger one ... the smaller one
decisions.reason: Readable names the two lights so that young readers know what is meant, though the Hebrew leaves them unnamed on purpose (m1).

decisions.choice: Literal gathers the whole verse under one final verb "ሠራ", so "and the stars" still comes last
decisions.reason: Amharic puts the verb at the end. Placing the one verb after the list keeps the Hebrew's single sentence and leaves the stars as the last, almost passing, item (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; honorific forms for God ("परमेश्वर ने", "उन्होंने")
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the English deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Hindi. Respect for God comes from the honorific third person at every level (style guide, section 7). The same through this passage.

hi.L: और दिन पर और रात पर शासन करें, और ज्योति और अंधकार के बीच विभाजन करें। और परमेश्वर ने देखा कि [वह] अच्छा [है]।
hi.B: दिन और रात पर शासन करें, और ज्योति को अंधकार से अलग करें। और परमेश्वर ने देखा कि यह अच्छा है।
hi.R: दिन और रात पर राज करें, और रोशनी को अँधेरे से अलग रखें। परमेश्वर ने देखा कि यह अच्छा है।

ru.L: и чтобы править днём и ночью, и чтобы проводить разделение между светом и тьмой. И Бог увидел, что [это] хорошо.
ru.B: чтобы управлять днём и ночью и отделять свет от тьмы. И Бог увидел, что это хорошо.
ru.R: чтобы управлять днём и ночью и держать свет отдельно от тьмы. Бог увидел, что это хорошо.

uk.L: і щоб панувати над днем і над ніччю, і щоб розділяти між світлом і темрявою. І побачив Бог, що [це] добре.
uk.B: щоб панували над днем і ніччю та відділяли світло від темряви. І побачив Бог, що це добре.
uk.R: щоб правили днем і ніччю і тримали світло окремо від темряви. Бог побачив, що це добре.

ja.L: 昼と夜を治めさせ、光と闇の間を分けさせられた。そして神は[それが]良いのを見られた。
ja.B: 昼と夜とを治めさせ、光と闇とを分けさせられた。神はそれを良いものとご覧になった。
ja.R: 昼と夜を治めさせ、光と闇とを分けておくようにされました。神は、それが良いものであるのをご覧になりました。

decisions.choice: to separate the light from the darkness: the lights take up the work of day one
decisions.reason: On the first day God himself separated the light from the darkness (verse 4). Now he gives that task to the lights he has made. Days one and four belong together, as do days two and five, and days three and six: the first three days shape the world, and the last three fill it.

decisions.choice: The purposes of verse 18 are closed with "ነው" ("it was so that ..."), bracketed at Literal
alternatives: moving the verb "set" of verse 17 to the end of verse 18
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the purposes follow the verb of verse 17. Amharic puts purpose clauses before their verb, so verse 17 ends with its verb and verse 18 adds the further purposes as "they are so that they rule ... and separate ...". This keeps each verse's content after its own number.

records.literal_gloss: And was evening and was morning, day fourth.

en.L: And there was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.
en.B: Evening came, and then morning: the fourth day.
en.R: Evening passed, and morning came. That was the fourth day.

es.L: Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana, un cuarto día.
es.B: Llegó la tarde, y después la mañana: el cuarto día.
es.R: Pasó la tarde y llegó la mañana. Ese fue el cuarto día.

fr.L: Et il y eut un soir et il y eut un matin, un quatrième jour.
fr.B: Le soir vint, puis le matin : le quatrième jour.
fr.R: Le soir est passé, puis le matin est venu. C’était le quatrième jour.

sw.L: Na kukawa jioni, na kukawa asubuhi, siku ya nne.
sw.B: Jioni ikaja, kisha asubuhi: siku ya nne.
sw.R: Jioni ikapita, asubuhi ikafika. Hiyo ilikuwa siku ya nne.

vi.L: Và có buổi chiều và có buổi sáng, ngày thứ tư.
vi.B: Chiều đến, rồi sáng đến: đó là ngày thứ tư.
vi.R: Buổi chiều qua đi, và buổi sáng đến. Đó là ngày thứ tư.

ko.L: 그리고 저녁이 있었고 아침이 있었다. 넷째 날이었다.
ko.B: 저녁이 지나고 아침이 되었다. 넷째 날이었다.
ko.R: 저녁이 지나고 아침이 왔다. 그렇게 넷째 날이 지나갔다.

pt.L: E houve tarde e houve manhã: um quarto dia.
pt.B: Veio a tarde, e depois a manhã: o quarto dia.
pt.R: A tarde passou, e a manhã chegou. Esse foi o quarto dia.

am.L: ምሽትም ሆነ፣ ጠዋትም ሆነ፤ አራተኛ ቀን።
am.B: ምሽት መጣ፣ ቀጥሎም ጠዋት መጣ፤ ይህ አራተኛው ቀን ነበር።
am.R: ምሽቱ አለፈ፤ ጠዋትም መጣ። ያ አራተኛው ቀን ነበር።

hi.L: और शाम हुई और सुबह हुई, चौथा दिन।
hi.B: शाम हुई, फिर सुबह: चौथा दिन।
hi.R: शाम ढली, और सुबह हुई। यह चौथा दिन था।

ru.L: И настал вечер, и настало утро: день четвёртый.
ru.B: Настал вечер, а потом утро: четвёртый день.
ru.R: Прошёл вечер, и наступило утро. Это был четвёртый день.

uk.L: І був вечір, і був ранок — день четвертий.
uk.B: Настав вечір, а потім ранок — четвертий день.
uk.R: Минув вечір, і настав ранок. Це був четвертий день.

ja.L: そして夕べがあり、そして朝があった。第四の日。
ja.B: 夕べが来て、それから朝が来た。四日目である。
ja.R: 夕方が過ぎて、朝が来ました。これが四日目でした。

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יִשְׁרְצ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם שֶׁ֖רֶץ נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֑ה וְעוֹף֙ יְעוֹפֵ֣ף עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֖י רְקִ֥יעַ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said God, let swarm the waters swarm[s] of living creature[s], and bird[s] let fly over the earth on [the] face of [the] vault of the heavens.

en.L: And God said, "Let the waters swarm [with] swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the vault of the heavens."
en.B: Then God said, "Let the waters teem with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the vault of the sky."
en.R: Then God said, "Let the water be full of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the sky."

es.L: Y dijo Dios: «Pululen las aguas [con] enjambres de seres vivientes, y vuelen aves sobre la tierra, por la faz de la bóveda de los cielos».
es.B: Entonces Dios dijo: «Que las aguas rebosen de multitudes de seres vivientes, y que las aves vuelen sobre la tierra, a lo ancho de la bóveda del cielo».
es.R: Entonces Dios dijo: «Que el agua se llene de seres vivos, y que las aves vuelen sobre la tierra, por el cielo».

fr.L: Et Dieu dit : « Que les eaux grouillent d’un grouillement d’êtres vivants, et que des oiseaux volent au-dessus de la terre, sur la face de la voûte des cieux. »
fr.B: Puis Dieu dit : « Que les eaux fourmillent d’une multitude d’êtres vivants, et que les oiseaux volent au-dessus de la terre, à travers la voûte du ciel. »
fr.R: Puis Dieu a dit : « Que l’eau soit pleine d’êtres vivants, et que des oiseaux volent au-dessus de la terre, dans le ciel. »

sw.L: Na Mungu akasema, "Maji yafurike makundi ya viumbe hai, na ndege waruke juu ya dunia, katika uso wa kuba la mbingu."
sw.B: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Maji yajae tele makundi ya viumbe hai, na ndege waruke juu ya dunia, katika kuba lote la anga."
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Maji yajae viumbe hai, na ndege waruke juu ya dunia, angani."

vi.L: Và Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Các dòng nước phải sinh sôi [đầy] những đàn sinh vật sống, và chim phải bay trên đất, ngang qua mặt vòm trời."
vi.B: Rồi Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Các dòng nước phải đầy dẫy những đàn sinh vật sống, và chim phải bay trên mặt đất, ngang qua vòm trời."
vi.R: Rồi Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Hãy để nước đầy những sinh vật sống, và hãy để chim bay trên mặt đất, ngang qua bầu trời."

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "물은 살아 있는 생물의 떼로 우글거려라. 그리고 새는 땅 위, 하늘 궁창의 표면 위를 날아라."
ko.B: 그때 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "물에는 살아 있는 생물이 떼를 지어 우글거리고, 새들은 땅 위로 하늘의 둥근 천장을 가로질러 날아라."
ko.R: 그때 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "물속에는 살아 있는 생물이 가득하여라. 땅 위 하늘에는 새들이 날아다녀라."

pt.L: E Deus disse: "Que as águas fervilhem [de] enxames de seres viventes, e que aves voem acima da terra, sobre a face da abóbada dos céus."
pt.B: Então Deus disse: "Que as águas se encham de multidões de seres vivos, e que as aves voem acima da terra, pela abóbada do céu."
pt.R: Então Deus disse: "Que a água fique cheia de seres vivos, e que as aves voem acima da terra, pelo céu."

am.L: እግዚአብሔርም አለ፦ «ውኆች በሕያዋን ፍጥረታት መንጋ ይርመስመሱ፤ ወፎችም ከምድር በላይ በሰማያት ጠፈር ፊት ላይ ይብረሩ።»
am.B: ከዚያም እግዚአብሔር «ውኆች በሕያዋን ፍጥረታት መንጋ ይርመስመሱ፤ ወፎችም ከምድር በላይ በሰማይ ጠፈር ላይ ይብረሩ» አለ።
am.R: ከዚያም እግዚአብሔር «ውኃው በሕያዋን ፍጥረታት ይሞላ፤ ወፎችም ከምድር በላይ በሰማይ ላይ ይብረሩ» አለ።

hi.L: और परमेश्वर ने कहा, "जल जीवित प्राणियों के झुंडों [से] उमड़ उठे, और पक्षी पृथ्वी के ऊपर आकाश के गुंबद के मुख पर उड़ें।"
hi.B: फिर परमेश्वर ने कहा, "जल जीवित प्राणियों के झुंडों से भर उठे, और पक्षी पृथ्वी के ऊपर आकाश के गुंबद में उड़ें।"
hi.R: फिर परमेश्वर ने कहा, "पानी जीवित प्राणियों से भर जाए, और पक्षी धरती के ऊपर आकाश में उड़ें।"

ru.L: И Бог сказал: «Пусть воды закишат роями живых существ, и пусть птицы летают над землёй по лицу свода небес.»
ru.B: Потом Бог сказал: «Пусть воды наполнятся множеством живых существ, и пусть птицы летают над землёй по своду неба.»
ru.R: Потом Бог сказал: «Пусть в воде будет полно живых существ, и пусть над землёй по небу летают птицы.»

uk.L: І сказав Бог: «Нехай закишать води кишінням живих істот, і нехай птахи літають над землею попід склепінням небес.»
uk.B: Тоді Бог сказав: «Нехай води закишать безліччю живих істот, і нехай птахи літають над землею попід небесним склепінням.»
uk.R: Тоді Бог сказав: «Нехай вода буде повна живих істот, і нехай птахи літають над землею по небу.»

ja.L: そして神は言われた。「水は生き物の群れで群がるように。そして鳥は地の上、天の天蓋の面を飛ぶように。」
ja.B: それから神は言われた。「水には生き物が群れをなしてうごめき、鳥は地の上、空の天蓋を飛び交うように。」
ja.R: それから神は言われました。「水の中は生き物でいっぱいになり、鳥は地の上の空を飛ぶように。」

decisions.choice: living creatures: beings that breathe and live
decisions.reason: The word often translated "soul" means a living, breathing being, or the life within it. The same words describe these animals and, in 2:7, the man ("a living being"). They do not set human beings apart from animals; what sets them apart is the image of God (verses 26-27).

decisions.choice: swarm: move in great numbers
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun both picture crowds of small creatures moving together, like shoals of fish. The waters are to teem with life.

decisions.choice: birds: flying creatures in general
decisions.reason: The word means any creature that flies, and comes from the verb "fly" in the same verse; elsewhere it includes winged insects (Leviticus 11:20). Here it is chiefly birds.

decisions.choice: swarm [with] swarms
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats the root as verb and object; Literal brackets the "with" English needs.

decisions.choice: seres vivientes (L, B); seres vivos (R)
decisions.reason: The words mean living, breathing beings (m1); "almas" would suggest a soul that sets humans apart, which is not the point here. "Seres vivientes" is the careful phrase used again for the animals and, in 2:7, for the man; Readable says "seres vivos", the everyday form.

decisions.choice: grouillent d'un grouillement
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one root for the verb and its object (m2). French can repeat it with "grouiller" and "grouillement", so Literal needs no bracketed "with"; Balanced says "fourmillent d'une multitude".

decisions.choice: "sinh vật sống" for nefesh chayyah
decisions.reason: The phrase means beings that breathe and live (m1); "linh hồn" (soul) would suggest more than the Hebrew says of animals.

decisions.choice: fervilhem [de] enxames
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the root as verb and object; Portuguese "fervilhar" needs "de" before what fills the waters, so Literal brackets it, as the English brackets "with".

decisions.choice: "ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት" (living creatures) at every level; "በ... መንጋ ይርመስመሱ" (swarm with swarms) at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: "ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት" says "beings that live and breathe" (m1) without the religious sense "soul" has for Amharic readers, and it covers fish as well as birds and beasts. "ይርመሰመሱ" is the verb for creatures moving in great numbers (m2), and "መንጋ" (a swarm, a flock) keeps the Hebrew's repetition of the root at Literal and Balanced; Readable says the water is full of them.

decisions.choice: "закишат роями"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the verb and the noun of the same root ("swarm swarms"). Russian "кишеть кишением" is not possible, so Literal pairs "закишат" with "рои", a word for creatures moving in great numbers (m2).

source.text: וַיִּבְרָ֣א אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־הַתַּנִּינִ֖ם הַגְּדֹלִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת כָּל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַֽחַיָּ֣ה׀הָֽרֹמֶ֡שֶׂת אֲשֶׁר֩ שָׁרְצ֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם לְמִֽינֵהֶ֗ם וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ע֤וֹף כָּנָף֙ לְמִינֵ֔הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: And created God the sea monsters the great, and every living creature the moving which swarmed the waters to their kind, and every bird of wing to its kind. And saw God that [it was] good.

en.L: And God created the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed, according to their kind, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that [it was] good.
en.B: So God created the great sea creatures and every kind of living thing that moves and teems in the waters, and every kind of winged bird. And God saw that it was good.
en.R: So God created the great creatures of the sea, and all the kinds of living things that swim in the water, and all the kinds of birds. God saw that it was good.

es.L: Y creó Dios las grandes criaturas marinas y todo ser viviente que se mueve, con que pululaban las aguas, según su especie, y toda ave alada según su especie. Y vio Dios que [era] bueno.
es.B: Así creó Dios las grandes criaturas del mar y toda clase de seres vivientes que se mueven y abundan en las aguas, y toda clase de aves aladas. Y Dios vio que era bueno.
es.R: Así Dios creó las grandes criaturas del mar, y toda clase de seres vivos que nadan en el agua, y toda clase de aves. Dios vio que era bueno.

fr.L: Et Dieu créa les grandes créatures marines et tout être vivant qui se meut, dont les eaux grouillèrent, selon leur espèce, et tout oiseau ailé selon son espèce. Et Dieu vit que [c’était] bon.
fr.B: Dieu créa donc les grandes créatures de la mer et toutes les espèces d’êtres vivants qui se meuvent et fourmillent dans les eaux, et toutes les espèces d’oiseaux ailés. Et Dieu vit que c’était bon.
fr.R: Ainsi, Dieu a créé les grands animaux de la mer, et toutes sortes d’êtres vivants qui nagent dans l’eau, et toutes sortes d’oiseaux. Dieu a vu que c’était bon.

sw.L: Na Mungu akaumba viumbe vikubwa vya baharini, na kila kiumbe hai kinachosogea, kile kinachojaa tele majini, kulingana na aina zake, na kila ndege mwenye mabawa kulingana na aina yake. Na Mungu akaona kwamba [ni] vyema.
sw.B: Basi Mungu akaumba viumbe vikubwa vya baharini, na kila aina ya kiumbe hai kinachosogea na kujaa tele majini, na kila aina ya ndege mwenye mabawa. Mungu akaona kwamba ni vyema.
sw.R: Basi Mungu akaumba viumbe vikubwa vya baharini, na aina zote za viumbe hai vinavyoogelea majini, na aina zote za ndege. Mungu akaona kwamba ni vizuri.

vi.L: Và Đức Chúa Trời sáng tạo các sinh vật lớn dưới biển và mọi sinh vật sống di động mà các dòng nước sinh sôi đầy dẫy, tùy theo loại của chúng, và mọi loài chim có cánh tùy theo loại của nó. Và Đức Chúa Trời thấy rằng [là] tốt đẹp.
vi.B: Vậy Đức Chúa Trời sáng tạo các sinh vật lớn dưới biển, mọi loại sinh vật sống di động đầy dẫy trong các dòng nước, và mọi loại chim có cánh. Và Đức Chúa Trời thấy điều đó là tốt đẹp.
vi.R: Vậy Đức Chúa Trời sáng tạo những sinh vật to lớn của biển, mọi loại sinh vật bơi lội trong nước, và mọi loại chim. Đức Chúa Trời thấy điều đó là tốt đẹp.

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 큰 바다 생물들과, 물에 우글거리는 움직이는 모든 살아 있는 생물을 그 종류대로, 그리고 날개 있는 모든 새를 그 종류대로 창조하셨다. 그리고 하나님께서 보시니 좋았다.
ko.B: 그래서 하나님께서 큰 바다 생물들과, 물속에서 우글거리며 움직이는 온갖 종류의 살아 있는 생물과, 날개 달린 온갖 종류의 새를 창조하셨다. 하나님께서 보시니 좋았다.
ko.R: 그래서 하나님께서 바다의 큰 생물들과, 물속을 헤엄치는 온갖 종류의 생물과, 온갖 종류의 새를 창조하셨다. 하나님께서 보시니 좋았다.

pt.L: E Deus criou os grandes animais do mar e todo ser vivente que se move, com que as águas fervilharam, conforme as suas espécies, e toda ave que tem asas conforme a sua espécie. E Deus viu que [era] bom.
pt.B: Assim Deus criou os grandes animais do mar e toda espécie de ser vivo que se move e fervilha nas águas, e toda espécie de ave que tem asas. E Deus viu que isso era bom.
pt.R: Assim Deus criou os grandes animais do mar, todos os tipos de seres vivos que nadam na água e todos os tipos de aves. Deus viu que isso era bom.

am.L: እግዚአብሔርም ታላላቆቹን የባሕር ፍጥረታት፣ ውኆቹ በየወገናቸው የተርመሰመሱባቸውን የሚንቀሳቀሱትን ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት ሁሉ፣ ክንፍ ያለውንም ወፍ ሁሉ እንደ ወገኑ ፈጠረ። እግዚአብሔርም መልካም [መሆኑን] አየ።
am.B: ስለዚህ እግዚአብሔር ታላላቅ የባሕር ፍጥረታትን፣ በውኆች ውስጥ የሚርመሰመሱትንና የሚንቀሳቀሱትን ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት ሁሉ በየወገናቸው፣ ክንፍ ያላቸውንም ወፎች ሁሉ በየወገናቸው ፈጠረ። እግዚአብሔርም መልካም መሆኑን አየ።
am.R: ስለዚህ እግዚአብሔር ታላላቅ የባሕር ፍጥረታትን፣ በውኃ ውስጥ የሚዋኙትን ሁሉንም ዓይነት ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት፣ ሁሉንም ዓይነት ወፎች ፈጠረ። እግዚአብሔር ጥሩ መሆኑን አየ።

hi.L: और परमेश्वर ने बड़े समुद्री जीवों को, और हर एक चलनेवाले जीवित प्राणी को, जिनसे जल उमड़ उठा, उनकी क़िस्म के अनुसार, और हर एक पंखवाले पक्षी को उसकी क़िस्म के अनुसार रचा। और परमेश्वर ने देखा कि [वह] अच्छा [है]।
hi.B: इस प्रकार परमेश्वर ने बड़े समुद्री जीवों को रचा, और जल में चलने-फिरने और झुंडों में भरनेवाले हर क़िस्म के जीवित प्राणी को, और हर क़िस्म के पंखवाले पक्षी को। और परमेश्वर ने देखा कि यह अच्छा है।
hi.R: तो परमेश्वर ने समुद्र के बड़े-बड़े जीव रचे, और पानी में तैरनेवाले हर क़िस्म के जीवित प्राणी, और हर क़िस्म के पक्षी। परमेश्वर ने देखा कि यह अच्छा है।

ru.L: И Бог сотворил больших морских существ и всякое живое существо, которое движется, которым закишели воды, по их виду, и всякую крылатую птицу по её виду. И Бог увидел, что [это] хорошо.
ru.B: Так Бог сотворил больших морских существ и все виды живых существ, которые движутся и кишат в водах, и все виды крылатых птиц. И Бог увидел, что это хорошо.
ru.R: Так Бог сотворил огромных морских животных и все виды живых существ, которые плавают в воде, и все виды птиц. Бог увидел, что это хорошо.

uk.L: І створив Бог великих морських істот і всяку живу істоту, що рухається, якою закишіли води, за їхнім видом, і всякого крилатого птаха за його видом. І побачив Бог, що [це] добре.
uk.B: Отож Бог створив великих морських істот і всі види живих створінь, що рухаються й кишать у водах, і всі види крилатих птахів. І побачив Бог, що це добре.
uk.R: Отже, Бог створив великих морських тварин і всі види живих істот, що плавають у воді, і всі види птахів. Бог побачив, що це добре.

ja.L: そして神は大きな海の生き物と、水が群がらせた動くすべての生き物を、種類に従って、また翼のあるすべての鳥を、種類に従って創造された。そして神は[それが]良いのを見られた。
ja.B: こうして神は、大きな海の生き物と、水の中に群がって動くあらゆる種類の生き物と、翼のあるあらゆる種類の鳥を創造された。神はそれを良いものとご覧になった。
ja.R: こうして神は、海の大きな生き物と、水の中を泳ぐあらゆる種類の生き物と、あらゆる種類の鳥をお造りになりました。神は、それが良いものであるのをご覧になりました。

decisions.choice: great sea creatures: the large animals of the sea
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the same word can name a snake (Exodus 7:9) or, in poetry, a sea monster that pictures powers opposed to God (Psalm 74:13; Isaiah 27:1). Here such creatures are simply part of what God has made, and they are good.

decisions.choice: created: the verb of verse 1, used again as animal life begins
decisions.reason: The verb used only of God appears here for the first time since verse 1, as the first living creatures are made. It comes again for human beings (verse 27).

decisions.choice: moves: creeps or glides, of creatures close to the ground or in the water
decisions.reason: The verb is used for small animals that move along the ground (verse 26), and here for the creatures that move through the water.

decisions.choice: every kind of
alternatives: according to their kind ... according to its kind
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable fold "according to its kind" into "every kind of" to keep a long list readable.

decisions.choice: toda clase de
decisions.reason: Where Balanced and Readable fold "according to its kind" into the list (as the English does), Spanish says "toda clase de", the idiom for "every kind of". "Especie" stays for the formula "según su especie".

decisions.choice: viumbe vikubwa vya baharini
decisions.reason: "Nyangumi" (whales) names one animal, and "joka" (a monster serpent) brings in the poetic sense of a power against God, which this verse does not have (m1). Swahili says "great creatures of the sea", as the English does.

decisions.choice: os grandes animais do mar
decisions.reason: "Monstros marinhos" would make them the hostile powers of poetry, which they are not here (m1); "baleias" names one animal. "Os grandes animais do mar" says what the English "great sea creatures" says.

decisions.choice: "ፈጠረ" (created) for the verb of verses 1, 21 and 27; "ሠራ" (made) for the everyday verb of making
decisions.reason: Genesis 1 uses two verbs: the one used only of God (verse 1, meaning decision m2 here) and the ordinary verb for making (verses 7, 16, 25, 26, 31). Amharic keeps them apart as "ፈጠረ" and "ሠራ", so the reader sees where the Hebrew uses the special verb.

decisions.choice: "बड़े समुद्री जीव" (L, B); "समुद्र के बड़े-बड़े जीव" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means the large animals of the sea (meaning decision); Hindi has no single word for them, and naming one animal would narrow it.

decisions.choice: "больших морских существ" (L, B); "огромных морских животных" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names the large animals of the sea (m1), not only fish. "Чудовища" would make them monsters, which this verse does not suggest.

records.literal_gloss: And blessed them God, saying, be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and the bird[s] let multiply on the earth.

en.L: And God blessed them, saying, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth."
en.B: God blessed them, saying, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters of the seas; and let the birds multiply across the earth."
en.R: God blessed them and said, "Have many young ones. Fill the water in the seas. And let there be more and more birds on the earth."

es.L: Y los bendijo Dios, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fecundos y {{plural_you:multiplíquense|multiplicaos}}, y {{plural_you:llenen|llenad}} las aguas en los mares, y que las aves se multipliquen sobre la tierra».
es.B: Dios los bendijo con estas palabras: «{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fecundos y {{plural_you:multiplíquense|multiplicaos}}; {{plural_you:llenen|llenad}} las aguas de los mares, y que las aves se multipliquen por toda la tierra».
es.R: Dios los bendijo y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} muchas crías. {{plural_you:Llenen|Llenad}} el agua de los mares. Y que haya cada vez más aves en la tierra».

fr.L: Et Dieu les bénit, disant : « Soyez féconds et multipliez, et remplissez les eaux dans les mers, et que les oiseaux se multiplient sur la terre. »
fr.B: Dieu les bénit en disant : « Soyez féconds et devenez nombreux, remplissez les eaux des mers ; et que les oiseaux se multiplient sur toute la terre. »
fr.R: Dieu les a bénis et leur a dit : « Ayez beaucoup de petits. Remplissez l’eau des mers. Et que les oiseaux soient de plus en plus nombreux sur la terre. »

sw.L: Na Mungu akawabariki, akisema, "Zaeni na mwongezeke, mjaze maji yaliyo baharini, na ndege wazidi kuongezeka juu ya dunia."
sw.B: Mungu akawabariki, akisema, "Zaeni mwe wengi, myajaze maji ya bahari; nao ndege wawe wengi kote duniani."
sw.R: Mungu akawabariki, akawaambia, "Zaeni kwa wingi. Jazeni maji ya bahari. Nao ndege wawe wengi zaidi na zaidi duniani."

vi.L: Và Đức Chúa Trời ban phước cho chúng, phán: "Hãy sinh sản và gia tăng, và làm đầy các dòng nước trong biển, và chim hãy gia tăng trên đất."

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 그것들에게 복을 주시며 말씀하셨다. "열매를 맺고 번성하여 바다의 물을 채워라. 그리고 새는 땅 위에서 번성하여라."
ko.B: 하나님께서 그것들에게 복을 주시며 말씀하셨다. "많이 낳고 불어나서 바다의 물을 가득 채워라. 새들도 땅 위에서 불어나라."

pt.B: Deus os abençoou, dizendo: "Sejam fecundos e multipliquem-se, encham as águas dos mares; e que as aves se multipliquem por toda a terra."
pt.R: Deus os abençoou e disse: "Tenham muitos filhotes. Encham a água dos mares. E que haja cada vez mais aves na terra."

hi.B: परमेश्वर ने उन्हें आशीष देकर कहा, "फलदायी हो और बढ़ो, और समुद्रों के जल को भर दो; और पक्षी पृथ्वी पर बढ़ते जाएँ।"

ru.L: И Бог благословил их, говоря: «Будьте плодовиты и умножайтесь, и наполните воды в морях, а птица пусть умножается на земле.»
ru.B: Бог благословил их, говоря: «Приносите потомство и умножайтесь, наполните воды морей; а птицы пусть умножаются по всей земле.»
ru.R: Бог благословил их и сказал: «Пусть у вас будет много детёнышей. Наполните воду в морях. А птиц пусть становится на земле всё больше и больше.»

uk.L: І благословив їх Бог, кажучи: «Будьте плідні й множтеся, і наповнюйте води в морях, а птахи нехай множаться на землі.»

uk.R: Бог благословив їх і сказав: «Майте багато потомства. Наповнюйте воду в морях. І нехай птахів на землі стає дедалі більше.»

ja.B: 神はそれらを祝福して言われた。「多くの子を生んで数を増やし、海の水に満ちなさい。鳥も地の上に数を増すように。」
ja.R: 神はそれらを祝福して言われました。「たくさんの子を生みなさい。海の水をいっぱいにしなさい。鳥も地の上でどんどん増えるように。」

decisions.choice: blessed: God gives them life and the power to increase
decisions.reason: To bless here is to give the gift of fruitfulness: God's blessing is the power to have young and to multiply. It is given to the sea creatures and birds, and then, in nearly the same words, to human beings (verse 28).

decisions.choice: Have many young ones
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "be fruitful and multiply" means for animals.

decisions.choice: ustedes forms by default (Sean, multiplíquense, llenen); vosotros forms with the setting (Sed, multiplicaos, llenad)
decisions.reason: God speaks to many creatures at once, so Spanish must choose a plural form of address. The default is the "ustedes" form used by most Spanish speakers; the plural-you setting gives the "vosotros" form of Spain, as in the New Testament. The same spans are used when God speaks to the man and the woman (verses 28-29).

decisions.choice: Sean fecundos y multiplíquense
decisions.reason: "Fecundos" names the gift of bearing young that the blessing gives (m1). "Fructificar" now sounds old-fashioned, and the familiar "Crezcan y multiplíquense" says "grow", which the Hebrew does not.

decisions.choice: bénir; Soyez féconds et multipliez (L); Soyez féconds et devenez nombreux (B)
decisions.reason: "Bénir" and "la bénédiction" are used for this word throughout the Pentateuch. Literal keeps the two verbs of the Hebrew as French has long said them; Balanced says "devenez nombreux", which a modern reader hears more plainly than an intransitive "multipliez". Readable follows the English (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: akawabariki
decisions.reason: "Kubariki", "baraka" are used for this word throughout the Pentateuch. The creatures are referred to with the animate class 2 object marker ("-wa-"), as Swahili does for animals, rather than the class 8 "-vi-" of "viumbe".

decisions.choice: "ban phước" for bless
decisions.reason: The word the project uses for God blessing throughout Genesis: God gives them life and the power to increase (m1). The command "be fruitful and multiply" is "Hãy sinh sản và gia tăng" wherever it returns (1:28; 9:1, 7).

decisions.choice: "복을 주시며"; "열매를 맺고 번성하여라" (L); "많이 낳고 불어나라" (B); "새끼를 많이 낳아라" (R)
decisions.reason: "Bless" is "복을 주다" throughout the book, as the terms note settles. The command pictures a plant bearing fruit; Literal keeps the picture, Balanced and Readable say what it means for animals. The older wording "생육하고 번성하라" belongs to older Bibles. The same words return in verse 28 and in chapters 8, 9 and 35.

decisions.choice: Sejam fecundos e multipliquem-se
decisions.reason: God addresses a group, so the verbs are in the plural of "vocês" (style section 4); the traditional "Crescei e multiplicai-vos" uses the "vós" forms, which are not used. "Sejam fecundos" keeps the image of bearing fruit; the same words return for human beings in verse 28.

decisions.choice: "ተዋለዱ፣ ብዙ" (breed and multiply) at Literal and Balanced, here and in verse 28 (and 9:1, 9:7); "ብዙ ተዋለዱ" (breed much) at Readable
decisions.reason: "ተዋለደ" is the ordinary Amharic verb for bearing young, which fits fish and birds as well as people, and "በዛ" is to become many; the third person is "ይዋለዱ፣ ይብዙ". Readable joins the two verbs, as the English Readable says "have many young ones". The familiar "ብዙ ተባዙ" of older versions is not used.

decisions.choice: "आशीष देना" (bless)
decisions.reason: The word for blessing used through the Pentateuch and the New Testament. God gives life and the power to increase (m1); "आशीर्वाद" is the everyday word for an elder's good wishes.

decisions.choice: "Будьте плодовиты и умножайтесь" (L); "Приносите потомство и умножайтесь" (B)
decisions.reason: The traditional phrase has become a fixed saying, often used jokingly. Literal says "be fruitful" plainly; Balanced says what it means. The same wording is used in 1:28, 9:1 and 9:7.

decisions.choice: "Будьте плідні й множтеся"
decisions.reason: The same pair of verbs returns in 1:28, 9:1, 9:7 and 35:11 and is kept the same each time; Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: "実を結び、数を増し" (L); "多くの子を生んで数を増やし" (B); "たくさんの子を生みなさい" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of bearing fruit; Balanced and Readable say what it means for living creatures. The well-known short form is avoided so that the sentence is composed afresh.

records.literal_gloss: And was evening and was morning, day fifth.

en.L: And there was evening and there was morning, a fifth day.
en.B: Evening came, and then morning: the fifth day.
en.R: Evening passed, and morning came. That was the fifth day.

es.L: Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana, un quinto día.
es.B: Llegó la tarde, y después la mañana: el quinto día.
es.R: Pasó la tarde y llegó la mañana. Ese fue el quinto día.

fr.L: Et il y eut un soir et il y eut un matin, un cinquième jour.
fr.B: Le soir vint, puis le matin : le cinquième jour.
fr.R: Le soir est passé, puis le matin est venu. C’était le cinquième jour.

sw.L: Na kukawa jioni, na kukawa asubuhi, siku ya tano.
sw.B: Jioni ikaja, kisha asubuhi: siku ya tano.
sw.R: Jioni ikapita, asubuhi ikafika. Hiyo ilikuwa siku ya tano.

vi.L: Và có buổi chiều và có buổi sáng, ngày thứ năm.
vi.B: Chiều đến, rồi sáng đến: đó là ngày thứ năm.
vi.R: Buổi chiều qua đi, và buổi sáng đến. Đó là ngày thứ năm.

ko.L: 그리고 저녁이 있었고 아침이 있었다. 다섯째 날이었다.
ko.B: 저녁이 지나고 아침이 되었다. 다섯째 날이었다.
ko.R: 저녁이 지나고 아침이 왔다. 그렇게 다섯째 날이 지나갔다.

pt.L: E houve tarde e houve manhã: um quinto dia.
pt.B: Veio a tarde, e depois a manhã: o quinto dia.
pt.R: A tarde passou, e a manhã chegou. Esse foi o quinto dia.

am.L: ምሽትም ሆነ፣ ጠዋትም ሆነ፤ አምስተኛ ቀን።
am.B: ምሽት መጣ፣ ቀጥሎም ጠዋት መጣ፤ ይህ አምስተኛው ቀን ነበር።
am.R: ምሽቱ አለፈ፤ ጠዋትም መጣ። ያ አምስተኛው ቀን ነበር።

hi.L: और शाम हुई और सुबह हुई, पाँचवाँ दिन।
hi.B: शाम हुई, फिर सुबह: पाँचवाँ दिन।
hi.R: शाम ढली, और सुबह हुई। यह पाँचवाँ दिन था।

ru.L: И настал вечер, и настало утро: день пятый.
ru.B: Настал вечер, а потом утро: пятый день.
ru.R: Прошёл вечер, и наступило утро. Это был пятый день.

uk.L: І був вечір, і був ранок — день пʼятий.
uk.B: Настав вечір, а потім ранок — пʼятий день.
uk.R: Минув вечір, і настав ранок. Це був пʼятий день.

ja.L: そして夕べがあり、そして朝があった。第五の日。
ja.B: 夕べが来て、それから朝が来た。五日目である。
ja.R: 夕方が過ぎて、朝が来ました。これが五日目でした。

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים תּוֹצֵ֨א הָאָ֜רֶץ נֶ֤פֶשׁ חַיָּה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ בְּהֵמָ֥ה וָרֶ֛מֶשׂ וְחַֽיְתוֹ־אֶ֖רֶץ לְמִינָ֑הּ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said God, let bring forth the earth living creature[s] to its kind, livestock and creeping thing[s] and animal[s] of earth to its kind. And was so.

en.L: And God said, "Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kind: livestock and creeping things and animals of [the] earth according to their kind." And it was so.
en.B: Then God said, "Let the earth bring forth living creatures, each according to its kind: livestock, creatures that move along the ground, and wild animals, each according to its kind." And so it happened.
en.R: Then God said, "Let the land be filled with living creatures of every kind: farm animals, small creatures that crawl, and wild animals." And that is what happened.

es.L: Y dijo Dios: «Produzca la tierra seres vivientes según su especie: ganado y seres que se arrastran y animales de [la] tierra según su especie». Y fue así.
es.B: Entonces Dios dijo: «Que la tierra produzca seres vivientes, cada uno según su especie: ganado, animales que se arrastran por el suelo y animales salvajes, cada uno según su especie». Y así sucedió.
es.R: Entonces Dios dijo: «Que la tierra se llene de seres vivos de toda clase: animales de granja, animalitos que se arrastran y animales salvajes». Y eso fue lo que pasó.

fr.L: Et Dieu dit : « Que la terre fasse sortir des êtres vivants selon leur espèce : bétail, et bêtes rampantes, et animaux de [la] terre selon leur espèce. » Et ce fut ainsi.
fr.B: Puis Dieu dit : « Que la terre fasse sortir des êtres vivants, chacun selon son espèce : du bétail, des bêtes qui se déplacent au ras du sol et des animaux sauvages, chacun selon son espèce. » Et il en alla ainsi.
fr.R: Puis Dieu a dit : « Que la terre se remplisse d’êtres vivants de toutes sortes : des animaux de la ferme, des petites bêtes qui rampent, et des animaux sauvages. » Et c’est ce qui s’est passé.

sw.L: Na Mungu akasema, "Nchi itoe viumbe hai kulingana na aina zake: wanyama wa kufugwa, na vitambaavyo, na wanyama wa nchi kulingana na aina zao." Na ikawa hivyo.
sw.B: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Nchi itoe viumbe hai, kila kimoja kulingana na aina yake: wanyama wa kufugwa, viumbe vinavyotambaa ardhini, na wanyama wa porini, kila kimoja kulingana na aina yake." Ndivyo ilivyokuwa.
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Nchi ijae viumbe hai vya kila aina: wanyama wa kufugwa, viumbe vidogo vinavyotambaa, na wanyama wa porini." Na hivyo ndivyo ilivyotokea.

vi.L: Và Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Đất phải sinh ra sinh vật sống tùy theo loại của chúng: gia súc, loài bò sát và thú vật của đất tùy theo loại của chúng." Và đã như vậy.
vi.B: Rồi Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Đất phải sinh ra các sinh vật sống, mỗi thứ tùy theo loại của nó: gia súc, loài bò sát và thú rừng, mỗi thứ tùy theo loại của nó." Và việc đã xảy ra như vậy.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Hãy để đất đầy những sinh vật sống đủ mọi loại: gia súc, những con vật nhỏ bò trên đất, và thú rừng." Và mọi việc đã xảy ra đúng như thế.

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "땅은 살아 있는 생물을 그 종류대로 내어라. 가축과 기어 다니는 것과 땅의 짐승을 그 종류대로 [내어라]." 그리고 그대로 되었다.
ko.B: 그때 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "땅은 살아 있는 생물을 저마다 종류대로 내어라. 가축과 땅 위를 기어 다니는 것과 들짐승을 저마다 종류대로 내어라." 그러자 그대로 되었다.
ko.R: 그때 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "땅에는 온갖 종류의 살아 있는 생물이 가득하여라. 집짐승과, 기어 다니는 작은 생물과, 들짐승이 생겨라." 그러자 그대로 되었다.

pt.L: E Deus disse: "Que a terra produza seres viventes conforme a sua espécie: animais domésticos e criaturas rastejantes e animais da terra conforme a sua espécie." E foi assim.
pt.B: Então Deus disse: "Que a terra produza seres vivos, cada um de acordo com a sua espécie: animais domésticos, criaturas que se movem rente ao chão e animais selvagens, cada um de acordo com a sua espécie." E assim aconteceu.
pt.R: Então Deus disse: "Que a terra se encha de seres vivos de todo tipo: animais de criação, pequenos animais que rastejam e animais selvagens." E foi isso que aconteceu.

am.L: እግዚአብሔርም አለ፦ «ምድር ሕያዋን ፍጥረታትን በየወገናቸው፣ ከብቶችንና በምድር ላይ የሚሳቡትን፣ የምድርንም አራዊት በየወገናቸው ታውጣ።» እንደዚያም ሆነ።
am.B: ከዚያም እግዚአብሔር «ምድር ሕያዋን ፍጥረታትን በየወገናቸው ታውጣ፤ ከብቶችን፣ በምድር ላይ የሚሳቡ ፍጥረታትንና አራዊትን፣ በየወገናቸው ታውጣ» አለ። እንደተባለውም ሆነ።
am.R: ከዚያም እግዚአብሔር «ምድር በሁሉም ዓይነት ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት ትሞላ፤ በቤት እንስሳት፣ በሚሳቡ ትናንሽ ፍጥረታትና በዱር አራዊት ትሞላ» አለ። የሆነውም ይኸው ነው።

hi.L: और परमेश्वर ने कहा, "पृथ्वी जीवित प्राणियों को उनकी क़िस्म के अनुसार उत्पन्न करे: घरेलू पशु और रेंगनेवाले जंतु और पृथ्वी के पशु, उनकी क़िस्म के अनुसार।" और ऐसा ही हुआ।
hi.B: फिर परमेश्वर ने कहा, "पृथ्वी जीवित प्राणियों को उत्पन्न करे, हर एक को उसकी क़िस्म के अनुसार: घरेलू पशु, ज़मीन पर रेंगनेवाले जंतु, और जंगली पशु, हर एक अपनी क़िस्म के अनुसार।" और ऐसा ही हो गया।
hi.R: फिर परमेश्वर ने कहा, "धरती हर क़िस्म के जीवित प्राणियों से भर जाए: पालतू जानवर, रेंगनेवाले छोटे जीव, और जंगली जानवर।" और ठीक वैसा ही हुआ।

ru.L: И Бог сказал: «Пусть земля произведёт живых существ по их виду: скот, и ползающих, и зверей земли по их виду.» И было так.
ru.B: Потом Бог сказал: «Пусть земля произведёт живых существ, каждое по своему виду: скот, существ, которые ползают по земле, и диких зверей, каждое по своему виду.» Так и произошло.
ru.R: Потом Бог сказал: «Пусть на земле появятся всякие живые существа: домашние животные, маленькие ползающие животные и дикие звери.» Так всё и случилось.

uk.L: І сказав Бог: «Нехай земля видасть живих істот за їхнім видом: худобу, і плазунів, і звірів землі за їхнім видом.» І сталося так.
uk.B: Тоді Бог сказав: «Нехай земля видасть живих істот, кожну за своїм видом: худобу, плазунів і диких звірів, кожного за своїм видом.» І так сталося.
uk.R: Тоді Бог сказав: «Нехай на землі будуть живі істоти всіх видів: свійські тварини, дрібні повзучі створіння і дикі звірі.» І так усе й сталося.

ja.L: そして神は言われた。「地は生き物を種類に従って生み出すように。家畜と這うものと地の獣を、種類に従って。」そしてそのようになった。
ja.B: それから神は言われた。「地はそれぞれ種類に従って生き物を生み出すように。家畜と、地の上を這うものと、野の獣を、それぞれ種類に従って。」そして、そのとおりになった。
ja.R: それから神は言われました。「地に、あらゆる種類の生き物が生まれるように。家畜も、地をはう小さな生き物も、野の動物も。」すると、言われたとおりになりました。

alignments.target_span: creatures that move along the ground

decisions.choice: livestock, creeping things and wild animals: the three groups of land animals
decisions.reason: The first word is used for the larger animals that people keep, such as cattle and sheep; the second for small animals that move close to the ground, including reptiles and insects; the third, "the living things of the earth", for wild animals. As with the plants, these are groups as people see them, not a scientific list.

decisions.choice: farm animals; small creatures that crawl
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the first two groups (m1).

decisions.choice: seres que se arrastran (L); animales que se arrastran por el suelo (B); animalitos que se arrastran (R)
decisions.reason: "Reptiles" names only one group of animals in Spanish. The Hebrew word covers all small creatures that move close to the ground, insects included (m1), so every level describes how they move.

decisions.choice: animais domésticos; criaturas rastejantes (L), criaturas que se movem rente ao chão (B) (R: animais de criação; pequenos animais que rastejam)
decisions.reason: "Gado" means cattle, narrower than the word for the larger animals people keep; "répteis" leaves out the insects and other small animals the second word includes (m1). Readable uses the plain words, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ከብቶች" (livestock), "በምድር ላይ የሚሳቡ" (creeping things, those that creep on the ground), "አራዊት" (wild animals) at Literal and Balanced; "የቤት እንስሳት", "የሚሳቡ ትናንሽ ፍጥረታት", "የዱር አራዊት" at Readable, through Genesis
decisions.reason: The three groups of land animals (m1) each have their Amharic word. "እንስሳት" alone would mean animals in general, so the tame animals are "ከብቶች" and, at Readable, "የቤት እንስሳት" (home animals). "አራዊት" are wild beasts. The creeping things are described by the verb, "those that creep", rather than "ተሳቢዎች", which now reads as the zoologist's "reptiles".

decisions.choice: "घरेलू पशु", "रेंगनेवाले जंतु", "पृथ्वी के पशु" / "जंगली पशु" (L, B); "पालतू जानवर", "रेंगनेवाले छोटे जीव", "जंगली जानवर" (R)
decisions.reason: The three groups of land animals (meaning decision): animals kept by people, small creatures that move along the ground, and wild animals. Literal keeps "animals of the earth"; Balanced and Readable say what is meant. The same words through Genesis.

decisions.choice: "ползающие" (L); "существа, которые ползают по земле" (B); "маленькие ползающие животные" (R)
decisions.reason: "Гады" now means vermin or vile people, and "пресмыкающиеся" means reptiles. The Hebrew word covers all the small creatures that move close to the ground (m1).

decisions.choice: "худоба", "плазуни", "звірі землі" (L), "дикі звірі" (B); Readable "свійські тварини", "дрібні повзучі створіння"
decisions.reason: The three groups of land animals (meaning decision m1) in the plain modern words; "гади" now sounds like an insult, and "плазуни" covers what creeps along the ground.

decisions.choice: "家畜", "這うもの" (L, B) / "地をはう小さな生き物" (R), "地の獣" (L) / "野の獣" (B) / "野の動物" (R)
decisions.reason: The verse names the three groups of land animals (m1); Japanese keeps three distinct words, writing 這う in kana at Readable.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֩ אֶת־חַיַּ֨ת הָאָ֜רֶץ לְמִינָ֗הּ וְאֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־רֶ֥מֶשׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֖ה לְמִינֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: And made God [the] animal[s] of the earth to its kind and the livestock to its kind and every creeping thing of the ground to its kind. And saw God that [it was] good.

en.L: And God made the animals of the earth according to their kind, and the livestock according to their kind, and every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind. And God saw that [it was] good.
en.B: God made the wild animals, each according to its kind, the livestock according to their kinds, and every creature that moves along the ground according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
en.R: So God made all the kinds of wild animals, farm animals and small creatures that crawl on the ground. God saw that it was good.

es.L: E hizo Dios los animales de la tierra según su especie, y el ganado según su especie, y todo lo que se arrastra sobre el suelo según su especie. Y vio Dios que [era] bueno.
es.B: Dios hizo los animales salvajes, cada uno según su especie, el ganado según su especie, y todos los animales que se arrastran por el suelo según su especie. Y Dios vio que era bueno.
es.R: Así Dios hizo toda clase de animales salvajes, animales de granja y animalitos que se arrastran por el suelo. Dios vio que era bueno.

fr.L: Et Dieu fit les animaux de la terre selon leur espèce, et le bétail selon son espèce, et toute bête qui rampe sur le sol selon son espèce. Et Dieu vit que [c’était] bon.
fr.B: Dieu fit les animaux sauvages, chacun selon son espèce, le bétail selon ses espèces, et toutes les bêtes qui se déplacent au ras du sol, chacune selon son espèce. Et Dieu vit que c’était bon.
fr.R: Ainsi, Dieu a fait toutes sortes d’animaux sauvages, d’animaux de la ferme et de petites bêtes qui rampent sur le sol. Dieu a vu que c’était bon.

sw.L: Na Mungu akawafanya wanyama wa nchi kulingana na aina zao, na wanyama wa kufugwa kulingana na aina zao, na kila kitambaacho ardhini kulingana na aina yake. Na Mungu akaona kwamba [ni] vyema.
sw.B: Mungu akawafanya wanyama wa porini, kila mmoja kulingana na aina yake, wanyama wa kufugwa kulingana na aina zao, na kila kiumbe kinachotambaa ardhini kulingana na aina yake. Mungu akaona kwamba ni vyema.
sw.R: Basi Mungu akafanya aina zote za wanyama wa porini, wanyama wa kufugwa, na viumbe vidogo vinavyotambaa ardhini. Mungu akaona kwamba ni vizuri.

vi.L: Và Đức Chúa Trời làm ra thú vật của đất tùy theo loại của chúng, và gia súc tùy theo loại của chúng, và mọi loài bò sát trên mặt đất tùy theo loại của nó. Và Đức Chúa Trời thấy rằng [là] tốt đẹp.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời làm ra thú rừng, mỗi thứ tùy theo loại của nó, gia súc tùy theo loại của chúng, và mọi loài bò sát trên mặt đất tùy theo loại của nó. Và Đức Chúa Trời thấy điều đó là tốt đẹp.
vi.R: Vậy Đức Chúa Trời làm ra mọi loại thú rừng, gia súc và những con vật nhỏ bò trên mặt đất. Đức Chúa Trời thấy điều đó là tốt đẹp.

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 땅의 짐승을 그 종류대로, 가축을 그 종류대로, 땅의 기어 다니는 모든 것을 그 종류대로 만드셨다. 그리고 하나님께서 보시니 좋았다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 들짐승을 저마다 종류대로, 가축을 종류대로, 땅 위를 기어 다니는 모든 것을 종류대로 만드셨다. 하나님께서 보시니 좋았다.
ko.R: 그래서 하나님께서 온갖 종류의 들짐승과 집짐승과, 땅 위를 기어 다니는 작은 생물들을 만드셨다. 하나님께서 보시니 좋았다.

pt.L: E Deus fez os animais da terra conforme a sua espécie, e os animais domésticos conforme a sua espécie, e toda criatura rastejante do solo conforme a sua espécie. E Deus viu que [era] bom.
pt.B: Deus fez os animais selvagens, cada um de acordo com a sua espécie, os animais domésticos de acordo com as suas espécies e toda criatura que se move rente ao solo de acordo com a sua espécie. E Deus viu que isso era bom.
pt.R: Assim Deus fez todos os tipos de animais selvagens, de animais de criação e de pequenos animais que rastejam no chão. Deus viu que isso era bom.

am.L: እግዚአብሔርም የምድርን አራዊት በየወገናቸው፣ ከብቶችንም በየወገናቸው፣ በመሬትም ላይ የሚሳበውን ሁሉ እንደ ወገኑ ሠራ። እግዚአብሔርም መልካም [መሆኑን] አየ።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር አራዊትን በየወገናቸው፣ ከብቶችን በየወገናቸው፣ በመሬት ላይ የሚሳቡትንም ፍጥረታት ሁሉ በየወገናቸው ሠራ። እግዚአብሔርም መልካም መሆኑን አየ።
am.R: ስለዚህ እግዚአብሔር ሁሉንም ዓይነት የዱር አራዊት፣ የቤት እንስሳትና በመሬት ላይ የሚሳቡ ትናንሽ ፍጥረታትን ሠራ። እግዚአብሔር ጥሩ መሆኑን አየ።

hi.L: और परमेश्वर ने पृथ्वी के पशुओं को उनकी क़िस्म के अनुसार, और घरेलू पशुओं को उनकी क़िस्म के अनुसार, और भूमि पर रेंगनेवाले हर एक जंतु को उसकी क़िस्म के अनुसार बनाया। और परमेश्वर ने देखा कि [वह] अच्छा [है]।
hi.B: परमेश्वर ने जंगली पशुओं को, हर एक को उसकी क़िस्म के अनुसार, घरेलू पशुओं को उनकी क़िस्म के अनुसार, और भूमि पर रेंगनेवाले हर एक जंतु को उसकी क़िस्म के अनुसार बनाया। और परमेश्वर ने देखा कि यह अच्छा है।
hi.R: तो परमेश्वर ने हर क़िस्म के जंगली जानवर, पालतू जानवर और ज़मीन पर रेंगनेवाले छोटे जीव बनाए। परमेश्वर ने देखा कि यह अच्छा है।

ru.L: И Бог создал зверей земли по их виду, и скот по его виду, и всякое ползающее [существо] земли по его виду. И Бог увидел, что [это] хорошо.
ru.B: Бог создал диких зверей, каждого по своему виду, скот по своим видам и всех существ, которые ползают по земле, каждое по своему виду. И Бог увидел, что это хорошо.
ru.R: Так Бог сделал все виды диких зверей, домашних животных и маленьких животных, которые ползают по земле. Бог увидел, что это хорошо.

uk.L: І зробив Бог звірів землі за їхнім видом, і худобу за її видом, і всякого плазуна землі за його видом. І побачив Бог, що [це] добре.
uk.B: Бог зробив диких звірів, кожного за своїм видом, худобу за її видами і всяке створіння, що плазує по землі, за його видом. І побачив Бог, що це добре.
uk.R: Отже, Бог зробив усі види диких звірів, свійських тварин і дрібних створінь, що повзають по землі. Бог побачив, що це добре.

ja.L: そして神は地の獣を種類に従って、家畜を種類に従って、土の上を這うすべてのものを種類に従って造られた。そして神は[それが]良いのを見られた。
ja.B: 神は、野の獣をそれぞれ種類に従って、家畜を種類に従って、土の上を這うすべてのものを種類に従って造られた。神はそれを良いものとご覧になった。
ja.R: こうして神は、あらゆる種類の野の動物と家畜と、地面をはう小さな生き物を造られました。神は、それが良いものであるのをご覧になりました。

decisions.choice: ground: the soil, the earth that is worked
decisions.reason: For the first time the account uses a second word for the earth: the ground, the soil that people work. It sounds like the word for the human being (adam) in the next verse, a link the story makes plain in 2:7, where God forms the man from the dust of the ground.

decisions.choice: le sol
decisions.reason: The account brings in a second word for the earth, the ground that is worked (m1). French keeps "la terre" for the first word and says "le sol" for this one, here and in Genesis 2-3, so that the reader can follow the two.

decisions.choice: ardhini
decisions.reason: The second word for the earth, the ground that is worked (m1), is "ardhi" in Swahili, here and in Genesis 2-3 ("mavumbi ya ardhi", 2:7), while "dunia" and "nchi" render the first word.

decisions.choice: o solo
decisions.reason: The account here uses its second word for the earth, the soil that is worked (m1). "O solo" keeps it apart from "a terra" in Literal and Balanced, so that the link with 2:7, where the man is formed from the dust of the ground, can be seen; Readable says "o chão".

decisions.choice: "መሬት" (ground, soil) for the ground, kept apart from "ምድር" (earth, land), through Genesis
decisions.reason: Hebrew has one word for the earth or land and another for the ground, the soil that is worked (m1). Amharic keeps them apart as "ምድር" and "መሬት", which matters from 2:5 on, where the human being is formed from the ground and set to work it.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים נַֽעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֛ם בְּצַלְמֵ֖נוּ כִּדְמוּתֵ֑נוּ וְיִרְדּוּ֩ בִדְגַ֨ת הַיָּ֜ם וּבְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם וּבַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּבְכָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וּבְכָל־הָרֶ֖מֶשׂ הָֽרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said God, let us make humankind in our image, according to our likeness, and let them rule over [the] fish of the sea and over [the] bird[s] of the heavens and over the livestock and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.

en.L: And God said, "Let {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}} make {{gender:humankind|man}} in {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}} image, according to {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}} likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over the livestock and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth."
en.B: Then God said, "Let {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}} make {{gender:human beings|man}} in {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}} image, to be like {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}. Let them rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the earth, and over every creature that moves along the ground."
en.R: Then God said, "Let {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}} make {{gender:people|man}} in {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}} image, to be like {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}. They will be in charge of the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, the farm animals, the whole earth, and all the small creatures that crawl on the ground."

es.L: Y dijo Dios: «Hagamos {{gender:a la humanidad|al hombre}} a {{deity_pronoun:nuestra|Nuestra}} imagen, según {{deity_pronoun:nuestra|Nuestra}} semejanza, y que dominen sobre los peces del mar, y sobre las aves de los cielos, y sobre el ganado, y sobre toda la tierra, y sobre todo ser que se arrastra sobre la tierra».
es.B: Entonces Dios dijo: «Hagamos {{gender:a los seres humanos|al hombre}} a {{deity_pronoun:nuestra|Nuestra}} imagen, para que se parezcan a {{deity_pronoun:nosotros|Nosotros}}. Que gobiernen sobre los peces del mar y las aves del cielo, sobre el ganado y toda la tierra, y sobre todos los animales que se arrastran por el suelo».
es.R: Entonces Dios dijo: «Hagamos {{gender:a las personas|al hombre}} a {{deity_pronoun:nuestra|Nuestra}} imagen, para que se parezcan a {{deity_pronoun:nosotros|Nosotros}}. Estarán a cargo de los peces del mar y de las aves del cielo, de los animales de granja, de toda la tierra y de todos los animalitos que se arrastran por el suelo».

fr.L: Et Dieu dit : « Faisons {{gender:l’humanité|l’homme}} à {{deity_pronoun:notre|Notre}} image, selon {{deity_pronoun:notre|Notre}} ressemblance, et qu’ils dominent sur les poissons de la mer et sur les oiseaux des cieux et sur le bétail et sur toute la terre et sur toute bête qui rampe sur la terre. »
fr.B: Puis Dieu dit : « Faisons {{gender:les êtres humains|l’homme}} à {{deity_pronoun:notre|Notre}} image, pour qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:nous|Nous}} ressemblent. Qu’ils règnent sur les poissons de la mer et sur les oiseaux du ciel, sur le bétail et sur toute la terre, et sur toutes les bêtes qui se déplacent au ras du sol. »
fr.R: Puis Dieu a dit : « Faisons {{gender:les humains|l’homme}} à {{deity_pronoun:notre|Notre}} image, pour qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:nous|Nous}} ressemblent. Ils auront la charge des poissons de la mer et des oiseaux du ciel, des animaux de la ferme, de toute la terre et de toutes les petites bêtes qui rampent sur le sol. »

sw.L: Na Mungu akasema, "Tuwafanye binadamu kwa sura {{deity_pronoun:yetu|Yetu}}, kulingana na mfano {{deity_pronoun:wetu|Wetu}}, nao watawale juu ya samaki wa bahari, na juu ya ndege wa mbinguni, na juu ya wanyama wa kufugwa, na juu ya dunia yote, na juu ya kila kiumbe kitambaacho juu ya nchi."
sw.B: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Tuwafanye binadamu kwa sura {{deity_pronoun:yetu|Yetu}}, wafanane {{deity_pronoun:nasi|Nasi}}. Wawe watawala wa samaki wa baharini na ndege wa angani, wa wanyama wa kufugwa na dunia yote, na wa kila kiumbe kinachotambaa ardhini."
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Tuwafanye binadamu kwa sura {{deity_pronoun:yetu|Yetu}}, wafanane {{deity_pronoun:nasi|Nasi}}. Watasimamia samaki wa baharini, ndege wa angani, wanyama wa kufugwa, dunia yote, na viumbe vidogo vyote vinavyotambaa ardhini."

vi.L: Và Đức Chúa Trời phán: "{{deity_pronoun:chúng ta|Chúng ta}} hãy làm nên loài người theo hình ảnh của {{deity_pronoun:chúng ta|Chúng ta}}, giống như {{deity_pronoun:chúng ta|Chúng ta}}, và họ hãy cai trị cá dưới biển và chim trên trời và gia súc và khắp đất và mọi loài bò sát bò trên đất."
vi.B: Rồi Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Chúng ta hãy làm nên loài người theo hình ảnh của {{deity_pronoun:chúng ta|Chúng ta}}, để họ giống như {{deity_pronoun:chúng ta|Chúng ta}}. Họ hãy cai trị cá dưới biển và chim trên trời, gia súc và khắp đất, và mọi loài bò sát trên mặt đất."
vi.R: Rồi Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Chúng ta hãy làm nên con người theo hình ảnh của {{deity_pronoun:chúng ta|Chúng ta}}, để họ giống như {{deity_pronoun:chúng ta|Chúng ta}}. Họ sẽ cai quản cá dưới biển và chim trên trời, gia súc, khắp mặt đất, và mọi con vật nhỏ bò trên đất."

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "우리가 우리의 형상으로, 우리의 모양을 따라 사람을 만들자. 그리고 그들이 바다의 물고기와 하늘의 새와 가축과 온 땅과 땅 위를 기는 모든 기어 다니는 것을 다스리게 하자."
ko.B: 그때 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "우리의 형상으로 사람을 만들어 우리를 닮게 하자. 그들이 바다의 물고기와 하늘의 새, 가축과 온 땅, 그리고 땅 위를 기어 다니는 모든 것을 다스리게 하자."
ko.R: 그때 하나님께서 말씀하셨다. "우리의 형상으로 사람을 만들어 우리를 닮게 하자. 그들이 바다의 물고기와 하늘의 새와 집짐승과 온 땅과, 땅 위를 기어 다니는 모든 작은 생물을 맡아 다스리게 하자."

pt.L: E Deus disse: "Façamos {{gender:a humanidade|o homem}} à {{deity_pronoun:nossa|Nossa}} imagem, conforme a {{deity_pronoun:nossa|Nossa}} semelhança, e que dominem sobre os peixes do mar e sobre as aves dos céus e sobre os animais domésticos e sobre toda a terra e sobre toda criatura rastejante que rasteja sobre a terra."
pt.B: Então Deus disse: "Façamos {{gender:os seres humanos|o homem}} à {{deity_pronoun:nossa|Nossa}} imagem, para que sejam semelhantes a {{deity_pronoun:nós|Nós}}. Que eles reinem sobre os peixes do mar e as aves do céu, sobre os animais domésticos e toda a terra, e sobre toda criatura que se move rente ao chão."
pt.R: Então Deus disse: "Vamos fazer {{gender:os seres humanos|o homem}} à {{deity_pronoun:nossa|Nossa}} imagem, para serem parecidos {{deity_pronoun:conosco|Conosco}}. Eles vão governar os peixes do mar e as aves do céu, os animais de criação, a terra inteira e todos os pequenos animais que rastejam no chão."

am.L: እግዚአብሔርም አለ፦ «ሰውን በመልካችን፣ እንደ አምሳላችን እንሥራ፤ በባሕር ዓሦች ላይ፣ በሰማያት ወፎች ላይ፣ በከብቶችም ላይ፣ በምድርም ሁሉ ላይ፣ በምድር ላይ በሚሳቡ ፍጥረታት ሁሉ ላይም ይሠልጥኑ።»
am.B: ከዚያም እግዚአብሔር እንዲህ አለ፦ «ሰውን በመልካችን፣ እኛን እንዲመስል እንሥራ። በባሕር ዓሦችና በሰማይ ወፎች ላይ፣ በከብቶችና በምድር ሁሉ ላይ፣ በመሬት ላይ በሚሳቡ ፍጥረታትም ሁሉ ላይ ይሠልጥኑ።»
am.R: ከዚያም እግዚአብሔር እንዲህ አለ፦ «ሰዎችን በመልካችን፣ እኛን እንዲመስሉ አድርገን እንሥራ። በባሕር ዓሦችና በሰማይ ወፎች ላይ፣ በቤት እንስሳትና በምድር ሁሉ ላይ፣ በመሬት ላይ በሚሳቡ ትናንሽ ፍጥረታትም ሁሉ ላይ ኃላፊዎች ይሆናሉ።»

ru.L: И Бог сказал: «Создадим человека по {{deity_pronoun:нашему|Нашему}} образу, по {{deity_pronoun:нашему|Нашему}} подобию, и пусть они властвуют над рыбами моря, и над птицами небес, и над скотом, и над всей землёй, и над всяким ползающим, что ползает по земле.»
ru.B: Потом Бог сказал: «Создадим человека по {{deity_pronoun:нашему|Нашему}} образу, подобным {{deity_pronoun:нам|Нам}}. Пусть люди властвуют над рыбами в море и над птицами в небе, над скотом и над всей землёй, и над всеми существами, которые ползают по земле.»

ja.B: それから神は言われた。「わたしたちのかたちに、わたしたちに似るように人を造ろう。そして彼らに、海の魚と空の鳥、家畜と全地、また地の上を這うすべてのものを治めさせよう。」

decisions.choice: let us: God speaks in the plural as he makes human beings
alternatives: God speaks to the heavenly beings around him
a plural of fullness or majesty
a first hint of more than one person in God
decisions.reason: Until now God has said "let there be". Here he speaks in the plural, and the next verse returns to the singular ("he created"). The plural has been read in several ways: God speaking to the heavenly beings who serve him (as in 1 Kings 22:19-20, and Isaiah 6:8, "who will go for us?"), a plural that expresses God's fullness, or God deliberating with himself. Christian readers have also seen in it a first hint of the Trinity, since the New Testament links the Son with creation (John 1:3). The text itself is clear that God alone creates (verse 27).

decisions.choice: humankind: human beings, male and female, not one man
decisions.reason: Adam is the Hebrew word for human beings in general; it becomes a personal name only later in the story (4:25; 5:1-3). Here it has no article, and the words that follow, "let them rule", and verse 27, "male and female", show that it means humankind as a whole.

decisions.choice: image and likeness: human beings resemble God and represent him
alternatives: two different things in the human being, such as body and soul
decisions.reason: An image is a statue or copy, and kings of the ancient world set up images of themselves to show where they ruled. A likeness is a resemblance. Together the two words say that human beings are made to resemble God and to represent him on the earth, which is why the next words give them rule over it. The same pair is used, in the other order, when Adam fathers a son "in his likeness, according to his image" (5:3).

decisions.choice: rule: govern, as a king rules
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a king's rule (1 Kings 5:4; Psalm 72:8). Human beings are to rule the living creatures as God's representatives, and the king described in Psalm 72 rules for the good of those in his care (Psalm 72:12-14).

decisions.choice: and over all the earth, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: and over all the wild animals of the earth (Syriac)
decisions.reason: In a list of animals "all the earth" stands out, and the Syriac translation reads "all the wild animals of the earth", which matches verses 24-25 and may be what was first written. The Hebrew text and the Septuagint have "all the earth", which is followed here.

decisions.choice: humankind (L), human beings (B), people (R); with the traditional setting, man
decisions.reason: The word means human beings of both sexes (m2), so the default is an inclusive word. The gender setting gives "man", the traditional English word in this sense.

decisions.choice: us, our (lowercase by default; Us, Our with the setting)
decisions.reason: God's pronouns are lowercase by default and capitalised with the setting, including "us" and "our" here, where God speaks of himself.

decisions.choice: to be like us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "according to our likeness" means (m3) in plain words.

decisions.choice: la humanidad (L), los seres humanos (B), las personas (R); with the traditional setting, el hombre
decisions.reason: The word means human beings of both sexes (m2), so the default is an inclusive word. The gender setting gives "el hombre", the traditional Spanish word in this sense. The span takes in the "a" that Spanish puts before a personal object, so that the setting reads "al hombre".

decisions.choice: Hagamos, with no span; nuestra, nosotros lowercase by default, Nuestra, Nosotros with the setting
decisions.reason: Spanish carries the "us" of "let us make" in the verb ending alone, so there is no pronoun there to capitalise. Where a pronoun is written ("nuestra imagen", "a nosotros"), the deity-pronoun setting capitalises it, as it does elsewhere where God speaks of himself. The span does not decide how the plural is read (m1).

decisions.choice: a nuestra imagen, según nuestra semejanza
decisions.reason: "Imagen" and "semejanza" render the two Hebrew words (m3). Literal keeps each with its own preposition, as the Hebrew does; the familiar saying "a imagen y semejanza" merges them into one phrase. Balanced and Readable say what the likeness means, "para que se parezcan a nosotros", as the English does.

decisions.choice: l'humanité (L), les êtres humains (B), les humains (R); with the traditional setting, l'homme
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): the word means human beings of both sexes (m2), and French "l'homme" is read less and less as including women, so the default is an inclusive word and the gender setting gives the traditional "l'homme". "Qu'ils dominent" and "qu'ils nous ressemblent" refer to humankind as a group with either wording.

decisions.choice: Faisons, with no span; notre, nous (Notre, Nous with the setting)
decisions.reason: The French imperative "Faisons" has no separate pronoun for the English "us", so it has no span; the deity pronoun setting goes on "notre" and on the object "nous" in "pour qu'ils nous ressemblent".

decisions.choice: kwa sura yetu, kulingana na mfano wetu
alternatives: kwa mfano wetu, kwa sura yetu
decisions.reason: "Sura" is the form or face of a person, which suits "image", a statue or copy; "mfano" is a likeness or resemblance (m3). Balanced and Readable say "wafanane nasi", "to be like us", as the English does.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:yetu|Yetu}}, {{deity_pronoun:wetu|Wetu}}, {{deity_pronoun:nasi|Nasi}}; binadamu with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Tuwafanye" carries "us" inside the verb, so the deity pronoun setting goes on the free possessives and on "nasi" (with us). "Binadamu" already means human beings of both sexes, and Swahili has no traditional word for humankind that the gender setting could offer instead, so there is no gender span (style guide).

decisions.choice: God says "chúng ta" (spanned mid-sentence; "Chúng ta" at the start)
decisions.reason: God speaks in the plural (m1). Vietnamese "chúng ta" (we, including the hearer) is the form a speaker uses calling others to act with him, as God does here; "chúng tôi" would shut the hearers out. It takes the deity_pronoun setting like God's "Ta".

decisions.choice: "loài người" (L, B), "con người" (R), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "loài người" and "con người" already mean human beings, male and female (m2); there is no second, male-only wording for a setting to switch to. "hình ảnh ... giống như" are the words this project uses for the image and likeness of God.

decisions.choice: "사람" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span such as 인류 or 사람 against 남자
decisions.reason: "사람" already means human beings, men and women alike (meaning decision m2), and is also the word a traditional reader expects, so Korean has nothing for the gender setting to change (style guide section 7). The same holds in verse 27 and through the book.

decisions.choice: "형상" and "모양" (L); "형상 ... 우리를 닮게" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms note settles "형상" for the image and "모양" for the likeness. Balanced and Readable say the second word as a verb, "to be like us", as the English Balanced and Readable do.

decisions.choice: a humanidade (L), os seres humanos (B, R); with the traditional setting, o homem
decisions.reason: The word means human beings of both sexes, not one man (m2), so the default is an inclusive word, as in the English; the gender setting gives "o homem", the traditional Portuguese word in this sense. Words that agree with it stay in the plural, as the Hebrew "let them rule" does.

decisions.choice: dominem sobre (L); reinem sobre (B); governar (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a king's rule (m4). Balanced says "reinem sobre", which keeps the picture of human beings ruling as God's representatives; "governar" is kept in this chapter for the lights of verses 16-18, which have a different verb, except at Readable, which uses the plainest word for both.

decisions.choice: "ሰው" (L, B) and "ሰዎች" (R) for humankind, with no gender span; "ፈጠረው" in verse 27 likewise
decisions.reason: The Amharic "ሰው" already means a human being, man or woman, and its plural "ሰዎች" means people; it is not the word for a male ("ወንድ"). So the English choice between "humankind" and "man" has nothing to change in Amharic, and the meaning stays as decision m2 says: human beings, male and female.

decisions.choice: "በመልካችን፣ እንደ አምሳላችን" (in our image, after our likeness); "ይሠልጥኑ" (let them have dominion) at Literal and Balanced, "ኃላፊዎች ይሆናሉ" (they will be in charge) at Readable
decisions.reason: "መልክ" (image, form) is used for the Hebrew image here and in 1:27, 5:3 and 9:6, and "አምሳል" (likeness, resemblance) for likeness, here and in 5:1, 3; together they say that human beings resemble God and represent him (m3). Hebrew uses the ordinary verb for making here, so Amharic says "እንሥራ", keeping "ፈጠረ" for verse 27 (see verse 21). "ይግዙ" would also read as "let them buy", so the verb of ruling (m4) is "ይሠልጥኑ", and "ሠልጥኑ" in verse 28.

decisions.choice: "मनुष्य" (L, B); "इंसान" (R), no gender span
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means human beings, male and female (meaning decision). Hindi "मनुष्य" and "इंसान" already mean a human being of either sex, so the choice the English setting offers ("humankind" or "man") is already made, and the Hindi has no span.

decisions.choice: "छवि" (image); "समानता" (likeness)
decisions.reason: "छवि" is an image or likeness that shows and represents someone, the sense meaning decision on image and likeness gives. God's "हम" is the plural the Hebrew has (meaning decision on "let us"), not added respect.

decisions.choice: "человек" (L, B), "люди" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Hebrew means human beings, male and female (m2). Russian "человек" already means a human being of either sex, and "люди" people, so Russian needs no gender setting where the English has one ("humankind" / "man").

decisions.choice: "Создадим" (L, B); "Сделаем" (R)
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew has the ordinary verb "make", not bara; "сотворить" is kept for bara (1:1), which follows in verse 27.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "людина" (L) and "люди" (B, R) already mean human beings, men and women alike
alternatives: a gender span as the English
decisions.reason: Ukrainian "людина" is not a word for a male, so the English choice between "humankind" and "man" does not arise (docs/ukrainian-style.md section 7); the same holds through chapters 1-5.

decisions.choice: "образ" and "подоба" (L), "подібні до нас" (B), "схожі на нас" (R)
decisions.reason: The two words of the Hebrew kept apart at Literal; Balanced and Readable say with a verb what the likeness means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "人" with no gender span, and no deity_pronoun span on "わたしたち"
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, male and female (m2), and Japanese 人 already says that, so there is nothing for the gender setting to switch. Japanese has no capitals, so the deity pronoun setting has no span (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: "かたち" for image and "似姿" (L) / "似るように" (B) for likeness; "わたしたち" for the plural
decisions.reason: かたち is the plain word for the form something bears and keeps image and likeness apart at Literal (m3). God speaks of himself as わたし in Japanese, so the plural here is わたしたち, leaving its sense open as the Hebrew does (m1).
