decisions.choice: three lines of poetry, each with "created"
decisions.reason: The verse is three lines of verse, each with the verb used only of God. The repetition marks the making of human beings as the high point of the account. The second line turns the first round ("created ... in his image", "in the image of God ... created") to stress the image of God.

decisions.choice: him ... them: humankind is one, and also many
decisions.reason: The second line says God created "him", singular, since humankind is one whole; the third says "them", plural, male and female. Both are said of the same humankind.

decisions.choice: male and female: both sexes, equally made in God's image
decisions.reason: The words name the two sexes, as they do of the animals in 6:19. The two together are humankind, both bear the image of God, and the blessing and the task of verse 28 are given to both.

decisions.choice: them (default); him (traditional setting)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pronoun is singular, "him", for humankind as one whole (m2). English "it" would sound as if humans were things, so the inclusive default says "them", as the next line does; the gender setting gives the literal "him".

decisions.choice: He created them to be like God
alternatives: in the image of God he created him
decisions.reason: Readable says what being made in the image of God means for a young reader (1:26, m3), having said "in his own image" in the first sentence.

decisions.choice: los (L, B) and Las (R) by default; lo (L, B) and Los (R) with the traditional setting
decisions.reason: As in English, the default says "them" for the singular Hebrew "him" (m2), and the gender setting gives "lo", agreeing with "el hombre". Spanish pronouns agree in gender with their noun, so in Readable, where the default noun is "las personas", the pronoun is "las" by default and "los" with the setting.

decisions.choice: varón y hembra (L); varón y mujer (B); hombre y mujer (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words are the plain terms for male and female, used of animals too (m3; 6:19). Spanish now says "macho" only of animals, so even Literal uses "varón", the word for a male human being, beside "hembra", which still names the female sex. Balanced and Readable use the nouns for a man and a woman.

decisions.choice: {{gender:la|le}} créa
decisions.reason: French can keep the singular pronoun of the Hebrew (m2) with either wording: "l'humanité ... il la créa" by default, "l'homme ... il le créa" with the traditional setting. The English default needs "them" (r-en-1); French does not, and the third line has the plural "les", as the Hebrew does. Balanced also keeps "l'humanité" so that the singular reads naturally.

decisions.choice: alimwumba ... aliwaumba (L, B); wa kiume na wa kike (L, B), wanaume na wanawake (R)
decisions.reason: Swahili keeps the Hebrew turn from "him" to "them" (m2) with the object markers "-m-" and "-wa-", since "binadamu" can be taken as one or many. "Mume na mke" means husband and wife; "wa kiume na wa kike" names the two sexes, as the Hebrew does (m3).

decisions.choice: "loài người" ... "họ" for "him ... them"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "him" of humankind as one, then "them" of the many (m2). Vietnamese repeats "loài người" for the one and says "họ" for the many, so no gender span is needed. "có nam có nữ" is the phrase of Matthew 19:4.

decisions.choice: "사람을 ... 그들을": the noun repeated where the Hebrew says "him", then "them"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "him" of humankind, then "them" (meaning decision m2). Korean "그를" would read as one man, so Korean repeats "사람" for the first and keeps "그들을" for the second, which still shows humankind as one and as many.

decisions.choice: a (default, with "a humanidade"); o (traditional setting)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pronoun is singular, for humankind as one whole (m2). Portuguese "a humanidade" is a singular noun, so Literal can keep the singular pronoun, "a criou", where the English Literal has to say "them"; the gender setting gives "o criou", with "o homem". Balanced follows "os seres humanos" with "os".

decisions.choice: à imagem de Deus
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "a imagem de Deus" at Literal and Balanced wherever the Hebrew has the word for image (m3 of 1:26), so that 5:1-3 and 9:6 can be seen to take it up. Readable says what it means, "parecidos com Deus", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: macho e fêmea (L); homem e mulher (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "macho e fêmea", the words the Hebrew also uses of the animals (m3); in Portuguese they sound zoological, so Balanced and Readable say "homem e mulher", which names both sexes plainly.

decisions.choice: "ፈጠረው ... ፈጠራቸው" (created him ... created them) at Literal and Balanced, as in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "him" of humankind and then "them" (meaning decision m2). In Amharic "ሰውን ... ፈጠረው" is the ordinary way to speak of the human being as one, and it includes women, so Literal and Balanced keep the shift from one to many without a gender span (see 1:26). Readable says "people" and "them" throughout, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "उसे" (him), no gender span
decisions.reason: Hindi "उसे" is singular but has no gender, so Literal and Balanced can keep the Hebrew singular, humankind as one, beside the plural "उन्हें" of the last line (meaning decision on him ... them), and the choice the English setting offers does not arise.

decisions.choice: "их" by default, "его" with the traditional gender setting
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "him" of humankind, then "them" (m2). As in the English, the default says "them", which is who is meant; the traditional setting keeps the Hebrew "him", which in Russian agrees with "человек".

decisions.choice: "її ... їх": the singular pronoun agrees with "людину" and the plural follows, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English span chooses between "them" and "him"; Ukrainian "людину ... її" is already one and many without naming a male (meaning decision m2), so the Hebrew's change from singular to plural comes through as it stands.

decisions.choice: "これを" ... "彼らを" (L); the pronouns left out (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "him" and then "them" of humankind, one and many (m2). Literal keeps the shift with the neutral これ for the one and 彼ら for the many; Japanese has no need of the English gender setting here.

records.literal_gloss: And blessed them God, and said to them God, be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and rule over [the] fish of the sea and over [the] bird[s] of the heavens and over every living thing that creeps on the earth.

en.L: And God blessed them, and God said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living thing that creeps on the earth."
en.B: God blessed them and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply. Fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, and every living creature that moves along the ground."
en.R: God blessed them and said to them, "Have children, so that there are more and more of you. Fill the earth and take charge of it. Rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, and over every living creature that moves on the land."

es.L: Y los bendijo Dios, y les dijo Dios: «{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fecundos y {{plural_you:multiplíquense|multiplicaos}}, y {{plural_you:llenen|llenad}} la tierra y {{plural_you:sométanla|sometedla}}, y {{plural_you:dominen|dominad}} sobre los peces del mar, y sobre las aves de los cielos, y sobre todo ser viviente que se arrastra sobre la tierra».
es.B: Dios los bendijo y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fecundos y {{plural_you:multiplíquense|multiplicaos}}. {{plural_you:Llenen|Llenad}} la tierra y {{plural_you:sométanla|sometedla}}. {{plural_you:Gobiernen|Gobernad}} sobre los peces del mar, las aves del cielo y todos los seres vivientes que se mueven por el suelo».
es.R: Dios los bendijo y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} hijos, para que cada vez haya más de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Llenen|Llenad}} la tierra y {{plural_you:háganse|haceos}} cargo de ella. {{plural_you:Gobiernen|Gobernad}} sobre los peces del mar y las aves del cielo, y sobre todos los seres vivos que se mueven por la tierra».

fr.L: Et Dieu les bénit, et Dieu leur dit : « Soyez féconds et multipliez, et remplissez la terre et soumettez-la, et dominez sur les poissons de la mer et sur les oiseaux des cieux et sur tout être vivant qui rampe sur la terre. »
fr.B: Dieu les bénit et leur dit : « Soyez féconds et devenez nombreux. Remplissez la terre et soumettez-la. Régnez sur les poissons de la mer, sur les oiseaux du ciel et sur tous les êtres vivants qui se déplacent au ras du sol. »
fr.R: Dieu les a bénis et leur a dit : « Ayez des enfants, pour devenir de plus en plus nombreux. Remplissez la terre et prenez-la en charge. Régnez sur les poissons de la mer et sur les oiseaux du ciel, et sur tous les êtres vivants qui se déplacent sur la terre. »

sw.L: Na Mungu akawabariki, na Mungu akawaambia, "Zaeni na mwongezeke, ijazeni dunia na kuitiisha, na mtawale juu ya samaki wa bahari na juu ya ndege wa mbinguni na juu ya kila kiumbe hai kitambaacho juu ya nchi."
sw.B: Mungu akawabariki, akawaambia, "Zaeni mwe wengi. Ijazeni dunia na kuiweka chini ya mamlaka yenu. Tawaleni samaki wa baharini, ndege wa angani, na kila kiumbe hai kinachotembea ardhini."
sw.R: Mungu akawabariki, akawaambia, "Zaeni watoto, ili mwe wengi zaidi na zaidi. Ijazeni dunia na kuisimamia. Tawaleni samaki wa baharini na ndege wa angani, na kila kiumbe hai kinachotembea juu ya nchi."

vi.L: Và Đức Chúa Trời ban phước cho họ, và Đức Chúa Trời phán với họ: "Hãy sinh sản và gia tăng, làm đầy đất và chinh phục nó, và cai trị cá dưới biển và chim trên trời và mọi sinh vật bò trên đất."
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời ban phước cho họ và phán với họ: "Hãy sinh sản và gia tăng. Hãy làm đầy đất và chinh phục nó. Hãy cai trị cá dưới biển, chim trên trời, và mọi sinh vật di động trên mặt đất."
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời ban phước cho họ và phán với họ: "Hãy sinh con cái, để các con ngày càng đông. Hãy làm đầy mặt đất và quản lý nó. Hãy cai quản cá dưới biển và chim trên trời, và mọi sinh vật di động trên đất."

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 그들에게 복을 주시고, 하나님께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "열매를 맺고 번성하여 땅을 채우고 그것을 정복하여라. 그리고 바다의 물고기와 하늘의 새와 땅 위에서 기어 다니는 모든 살아 있는 것을 다스려라."
ko.B: 하나님께서 그들에게 복을 주시며 말씀하셨다. "많이 낳고 불어나라. 땅을 가득 채우고 정복하여라. 바다의 물고기와 하늘의 새와 땅 위를 움직이는 모든 생물을 다스려라."
ko.R: 하나님께서 그들에게 복을 주시며 말씀하셨다. "자녀를 많이 낳아서 수가 점점 더 많아져라. 땅을 가득 채우고 땅을 맡아 다스려라. 바다의 물고기와 하늘의 새와 땅 위에서 움직이는 모든 생물을 다스려라."

pt.L: E Deus os abençoou, e Deus lhes disse: "Sejam fecundos e multipliquem-se, e encham a terra e submetam-na, e dominem sobre os peixes do mar e sobre as aves dos céus e sobre todo ser vivo que rasteja sobre a terra."
pt.B: Deus os abençoou e lhes disse: "Sejam fecundos e multipliquem-se. Encham a terra e submetam-na. Reinem sobre os peixes do mar, as aves do céu e todo ser vivo que se move rente ao chão."
pt.R: Deus os abençoou e disse a eles: "Tenham filhos, para que vocês sejam cada vez mais numerosos. Encham a terra e assumam o controle dela. Governem os peixes do mar e as aves do céu e todos os seres vivos que se movem na terra."

am.L: እግዚአብሔርም ባረካቸው፤ እግዚአብሔርም አላቸው፦ «ተዋለዱ፣ ብዙም፤ ምድርንም ሙሏት፣ አስገዟትም፤ በባሕር ዓሦች ላይ፣ በሰማያት ወፎች ላይ፣ በምድር ላይ በሚሳብ ሕያው ነገር ሁሉ ላይም ሠልጥኑ።»
am.B: እግዚአብሔር ባረካቸው፤ እንዲህም አላቸው፦ «ተዋለዱ፣ ብዙ። ምድርን ሙሏት፤ አስገዟትም። በባሕር ዓሦች፣ በሰማይ ወፎችና በምድር ላይ በሚንቀሳቀሱ ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት ሁሉ ላይ ሠልጥኑ።»
am.R: እግዚአብሔር ባረካቸው፤ እንዲህም አላቸው፦ «ልጆችን ውለዱ፤ ቁጥራችሁም እየበዛ ይሂድ። ምድርን ሙሏት፤ ተቆጣጠሯትም። የባሕር ዓሦችን፣ የሰማይ ወፎችንና በምድር ላይ የሚንቀሳቀሱትን ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት ሁሉ አስተዳድሩ።»

hi.L: और परमेश्वर ने उन्हें आशीष दी, और परमेश्वर ने उनसे कहा, "फलदायी हो और बढ़ो और पृथ्वी को भर दो और उसे अपने वश में करो, और समुद्र की मछलियों पर और आकाश के पक्षियों पर और पृथ्वी पर रेंगनेवाले हर एक जीवित प्राणी पर अधिकार रखो।"

hi.R: परमेश्वर ने उन्हें आशीष दी और उनसे कहा, "बच्चे पैदा करो, ताकि तुम्हारी गिनती बढ़ती जाए। धरती को भर दो और उसे सँभालो। समुद्र की मछलियों और आकाश के पक्षियों पर, और ज़मीन पर चलनेवाले हर एक जीवित प्राणी पर राज करो।"

ru.L: И Бог благословил их, и Бог сказал им: «Будьте плодовиты и умножайтесь, и наполните землю, и покорите её, и властвуйте над рыбами моря, и над птицами небес, и над всяким живым [существом], ползающим по земле.»

decisions.choice: God said to them: the blessing is spoken to human beings directly
decisions.reason: The sea creatures and birds were blessed in the third person (verse 22). Human beings are spoken to: "God said to them". The blessing is the same, with a task added.

decisions.choice: subdue: bring under control
decisions.reason: The verb is strong: it is used for bringing a land under control (Numbers 32:22; Joshua 18:1) and for forcing people into service (Jeremiah 34:11). Here the earth is to be brought under human care and use, in a world God has just called good; in the next chapter the man is placed in the garden "to work it and keep it" (2:15).

decisions.choice: Have children, so that there are more and more of you
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "be fruitful and multiply" means for people.

decisions.choice: take charge of it
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer phrase for "subdue" (m2).

decisions.choice: ustedes forms by default (Sean, llenen, sométanla, ustedes); vosotros forms with the setting (Sed, llenad, sometedla, vosotros)
decisions.reason: God now speaks to the man and the woman directly (m1). As in verse 22, the default is the "ustedes" form and the plural-you setting gives the "vosotros" form; every verb and pronoun of address carries a span. "Les dijo" ("said to them") is the narrator's third person and has none.

decisions.choice: God calls them "các con" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Genesis terms note says, God speaking calls people "ngươi" at Literal and "con" at Balanced and Readable; here only Readable needs a pronoun.

decisions.choice: "አስገዟት" (subdue it) at Literal and Balanced; "ተቆጣጠሯት" (take charge of it) at Readable
decisions.reason: "አስገዛ" is to bring under control (m2). Readable uses the everyday "ተቆጣጠረ", as the English Readable says "take charge of it". God speaks to the man and woman together, so the verbs are plural ("እናንተ").

decisions.choice: God says "तुम" to people
decisions.reason: Through the Pentateuch God speaking to people says तुम, to one person or many, as Jesus does in the New Testament; people praying to God say तू.

decisions.choice: I give: a gift made in the act of speaking
decisions.reason: The verb has a completed form, used here, as often in the Bible, for an act done by the very words that announce it: by saying it, God gives it.

decisions.choice: for food: the first gift of food is plants and fruit
decisions.reason: In this account human beings and animals are given plants to eat (verses 29-30). After the flood God also gives animals as food (9:3), with a limit. The text says no more about how people or animals lived before then.

decisions.choice: Look (L, R); Here (B)
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what follows. Older English Bibles say "behold". Balanced says "here", as one does when handing something over.

decisions.choice: Miren (L, R); Aquí ... doy (B)
decisions.reason: "He aquí" is now archaic. Literal and Readable draw attention with "miren", addressed to the two of them (a plural-you span); Balanced says "aquí les doy", as one does when handing something over.

decisions.choice: Tenez
decisions.reason: As the English "Here" (r-en-1): "Tenez" is what French says when handing something over, which suits a gift made in the act of speaking (m1). Literal keeps "Voici", Readable "Regardez !".

decisions.choice: nawapa (L); ninawapa (B, R); Pokeeni (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew perfect here is a gift made by the very words that announce it (m1), which Swahili says with the present "nawapa", "I give you"; "nimewapa" would report a gift already made. Balanced opens with "Pokeeni", "receive", as the English says "Here".

decisions.choice: God says "Ta" and calls them "các ngươi" (L), "các con" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Genesis terms note says for the whole book: God speaking says "Ta" (with the deity_pronoun setting mid-sentence) and calls people "ngươi" at Literal and "con" at Balanced and Readable, as a father speaks.

decisions.choice: Vejam (L, R); Aqui está (B)
decisions.reason: "Eis que" is the older Bible form and reads as archaic; God speaks to the man and the woman together, so the verb is the plural "Vejam". Balanced says "Aqui está", as one does when handing something over, as the English Balanced says "Here".

decisions.choice: "እነሆ" (look) at Literal; "ይኸው" (here it is) at Balanced; "ተመልከቱ!" (look!) at Readable
decisions.reason: As in the Amharic New Testament, "እነሆ" is kept for Literal. Balanced uses "ይኸው", what an Amharic speaker says when handing something over, which fits a gift made as it is spoken (m1); Readable says "look!" to the hearers.

decisions.choice: "Вот" (L, B); "Смотрите!" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "look" draws attention to the gift made as God speaks (m1). Russian "вот" does this in a sentence; Readable says it as a call to look.

fr.L: et à tout animal de la terre et à tout oiseau des cieux et à tout ce qui rampe sur la terre, dans lequel [il y a] une vie vivante, [je donne] toute plante verte pour nourriture. » Et ce fut ainsi.
fr.B: et pour tous les animaux sauvages, tous les oiseaux du ciel et toutes les bêtes qui se déplacent sur le sol, pour tout ce qui a la vie en soi, les plantes vertes serviront de nourriture. » Et il en alla ainsi.
fr.R: Et tous les animaux sauvages, les oiseaux du ciel et les petites bêtes qui rampent sur le sol, tout ce qui vit, pourront manger les plantes vertes. » Et c’est ce qui s’est passé.

sw.L: na kwa kila mnyama wa dunia na kwa kila ndege wa mbinguni na kwa kila kitambaacho juu ya dunia, ambacho ndani yake [kuna] uhai, [ninawapa] kila mmea wa kijani kuwa chakula." Na ikawa hivyo.
sw.B: na kwa wanyama wote wa porini, ndege wote wa angani, na viumbe vyote vinavyotambaa ardhini, kwa kila chenye uhai ndani yake, mimea ya kijani itakuwa chakula." Ndivyo ilivyokuwa.
sw.R: Nao wanyama wote wa porini, ndege wa angani, na viumbe vidogo vinavyotambaa ardhini, kila kilicho hai, wanaweza kula mimea ya kijani." Na hivyo ndivyo ilivyotokea.

vi.L: và cho mọi thú vật của đất và cho mọi chim trên trời và cho mọi [vật] bò trên đất, có sự sống ở trong nó, [{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban] mọi cây cỏ xanh làm thức ăn." Và đã như vậy.
vi.B: và cho mọi thú rừng, mọi chim trên trời và mọi sinh vật di động trên mặt đất, mọi loài có sự sống, cây cỏ xanh sẽ là thức ăn." Và việc đã xảy ra như vậy.
vi.R: Còn mọi thú rừng, chim trên trời, và những con vật nhỏ bò trên đất, tức là mọi loài có sự sống, đều có thể ăn cây cỏ xanh." Và mọi việc đã xảy ra đúng như thế.

ko.L: 그리고 땅의 모든 짐승과 하늘의 모든 새와 땅 위를 기어 다니는 모든 [것], 곧 그 안에 살아 있는 목숨이 있는 것에게는 모든 푸른 풀을 먹을거리로 [준다]." 그리고 그대로 되었다.
ko.B: 또 모든 들짐승과 하늘의 모든 새와 땅 위를 움직이는 모든 생물, 곧 생명이 있는 모든 것에게는 푸른 풀이 먹을거리가 될 것이다." 그러자 그대로 되었다.
ko.R: 그리고 모든 들짐승과 하늘의 새와 땅 위를 기어 다니는 작은 생물들, 곧 살아 있는 모든 것은 푸른 풀을 먹을 수 있다." 그러자 그대로 되었다.

pt.L: e a todo animal da terra e a toda ave dos céus e a todo [ser] que rasteja sobre a terra, em que [há] um ser vivente, [eu dou] toda planta verde como alimento." E foi assim.
pt.B: e, para todo animal selvagem, toda ave do céu e toda criatura que se move rente ao chão, para tudo o que tem vida, as plantas verdes serão alimento." E assim aconteceu.
pt.R: E todos os animais selvagens, as aves do céu e os pequenos animais que rastejam no chão, todo ser vivo, podem comer as plantas verdes." E foi isso que aconteceu.

am.L: ለምድር አራዊት ሁሉ፣ ለሰማያት ወፎች ሁሉ፣ በምድር ላይ ለሚሳብ፣ ሕያው ነፍስ ላለበት ሁሉ፣ ለምለሙን ተክል ሁሉ ምግብ እንዲሆን [ሰጠኋቸው]።» እንደዚያም ሆነ።
am.B: ለአራዊት ሁሉ፣ ለሰማይ ወፎች ሁሉና በምድር ላይ ለሚንቀሳቀሱ ፍጥረታት ሁሉ፣ ሕይወት ላለው ሁሉ ደግሞ ለምለም ተክሎች ምግብ ይሆናሉ።» እንደተባለውም ሆነ።
am.R: የዱር አራዊት ሁሉ፣ የሰማይ ወፎችና በመሬት ላይ የሚሳቡ ትናንሽ ፍጥረታት፣ ሕይወት ያለው ሁሉ ለምለሙን ተክል መብላት ይችላሉ።» የሆነውም ይኸው ነው።

hi.L: और पृथ्वी के हर एक पशु को और आकाश के हर एक पक्षी को और पृथ्वी पर रेंगनेवाले हर एक [जंतु] को, जिसमें जीवित प्राण [है], [मैं] हर एक हरा पौधा भोजन के लिए [देता हूँ]।" और ऐसा ही हुआ।
hi.B: और हर एक जंगली पशु, आकाश के हर एक पक्षी, और ज़मीन पर रेंगनेवाले हर एक जंतु के लिए, अर्थात् हर उस प्राणी के लिए जिसमें जीवन है, हरे पौधे भोजन होंगे।" और ऐसा ही हो गया।
hi.R: और सब जंगली जानवर, आकाश के पक्षी, और ज़मीन पर रेंगनेवाले छोटे जीव, यानी हर जीवित प्राणी, हरे पौधे खा सकते हैं।" और ठीक वैसा ही हुआ।

ru.L: и всякому зверю земли, и всякой птице небес, и всякому [существу], ползающему по земле, в котором живая душа, [{{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} даю] всякую зелёную траву в пищу.» И было так.
ru.B: а всем диким зверям, всем птицам в небе и всем существам, которые движутся по земле, всему, в чём есть жизнь, пищей будут зелёные растения.» Так и произошло.
ru.R: А все дикие звери, птицы в небе и маленькие животные, которые ползают по земле, — все живые существа — могут есть зелёные растения.» Так всё и случилось.

uk.L: а всякому звірові землі, і всякому птахові небес, і всякому [створінню], що плазує по землі, у якому [є] жива душа, — [я даю] всяку зелену рослину на їжу.» І сталося так.
uk.B: а для всіх диких звірів, для всіх птахів у небі й для всіх створінь, що плазують по землі, для всього, що має в собі життя, їжею буде зелена рослинність.» І так сталося.
uk.R: А всі дикі звірі, птахи в небі й дрібні створіння, що повзають по землі, — усе живе — можуть їсти зелені рослини.» І так усе й сталося.

ja.L: また地のすべての獣と天のすべての鳥と、地の上を這うもので命の息のあるすべてのものには、すべての緑の草を食物として[与える]。」そしてそのようになった。
ja.B: また、地のすべての獣と空のすべての鳥と、地の上を這うもの、すなわち命の息のあるすべてのものには、緑の草が食物となる。」そして、そのとおりになった。
ja.R: また、すべての野の動物も、空の鳥も、地面をはう小さな生き物も、生きているものはみな、緑の草を食べてよい。」すると、言われたとおりになりました。

decisions.choice: every green plant for food: the verb carries over from verse 29
decisions.reason: This part of God's words has no verb of its own; "I give" carries over from verse 29.

decisions.choice: living life: the breath of life that animals have
decisions.reason: These are the words for "living creatures" in verses 20 and 24, used here of the life within the animals.

decisions.choice: [thing], [there is], [I give]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs that the Hebrew leaves to be understood (m1).

decisions.choice: em que [há] um ser vivente
decisions.reason: The words are those of "seres viventes" in verses 20 and 24 (m2); Literal repeats "ser vivente" so that the link can be seen, since "vida vivente", the English Literal's "living life", is not Portuguese.

decisions.choice: "ሕያው ነፍስ" (living life) and the bracketed verb "[ሰጠኋቸው]" (I have given them) at Literal
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase for the breath of life that animals have (m2) and brackets the verb that carries over from verse 29 (m1), as the English Literal brackets "[I give]".

decisions.choice: "живая душа"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional "живая душа" for the Hebrew "living life", as 1 Corinthians 15:45 does at Literal; Balanced and Readable say that it has life in it (m2).

decisions.choice: "жива душа" for the living life in animals
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase as the Ukrainian Bible tradition says it, "душа" meaning a living being, not a soul apart from the body; Balanced and Readable say "життя".

source.text: וַיַּ֤רְא אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְהִנֵּה־ט֖וֹב מְאֹ֑ד וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם הַשִּׁשִּֽׁי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And saw God all that he had made, and look, good very. And was evening and was morning, day the sixth.

en.L: And God saw all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made, and look, [it was] very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.
en.B: God looked at everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made, and it was very good indeed. Evening came, and then morning: the sixth day.
en.R: God looked at everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made, and it was very good. Evening passed, and morning came. That was the sixth day.

es.L: Y vio Dios todo lo que había hecho, y mira, [era] muy bueno. Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana, el sexto día.
es.B: Dios miró todo lo que había hecho, y era realmente muy bueno. Llegó la tarde, y después la mañana: el sexto día.
es.R: Dios miró todo lo que había hecho, y era muy bueno. Pasó la tarde y llegó la mañana. Ese fue el sexto día.

fr.L: Et Dieu vit tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait, et voici, [c’était] très bon. Et il y eut un soir et il y eut un matin, le sixième jour.
fr.B: Dieu regarda tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait, et c’était vraiment très bon. Le soir vint, puis le matin : le sixième jour.
fr.R: Dieu a regardé tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait, et c’était très bon. Le soir est passé, puis le matin est venu. C’était le sixième jour.

sw.L: Na Mungu akaona kila kitu alichokuwa amekifanya, na tazama, [kilikuwa] chema mno. Na kukawa jioni, na kukawa asubuhi, siku ya sita.
sw.B: Mungu akatazama kila kitu alichokuwa amefanya, na kweli kilikuwa chema mno. Jioni ikaja, kisha asubuhi: siku ya sita.
sw.R: Mungu akatazama kila kitu alichokuwa amefanya, nacho kilikuwa kizuri sana. Jioni ikapita, asubuhi ikafika. Hiyo ilikuwa siku ya sita.

vi.L: Và Đức Chúa Trời thấy mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm ra, và này, [là] rất tốt đẹp. Và có buổi chiều và có buổi sáng, ngày thứ sáu.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời nhìn mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm ra, và thật là rất tốt đẹp. Chiều đến, rồi sáng đến: đó là ngày thứ sáu.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời nhìn mọi vật {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm ra, và mọi vật đều rất tốt đẹp. Buổi chiều qua đi, và buổi sáng đến. Đó là ngày thứ sáu.

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 자신이 만드신 모든 것을 보셨는데, 보아라, 매우 좋았다. 그리고 저녁이 있었고 아침이 있었다. 여섯째 날이었다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 만드신 모든 것을 보시니, 참으로 매우 좋았다. 저녁이 지나고 아침이 되었다. 여섯째 날이었다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 만드신 모든 것을 보시니 아주 좋았다. 저녁이 지나고 아침이 왔다. 그렇게 여섯째 날이 지나갔다.

pt.L: E Deus viu tudo o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha feito, e eis que [era] muito bom. E houve tarde e houve manhã: o sexto dia.
pt.B: Deus olhou para tudo o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha feito, e era realmente muito bom. Veio a tarde, e depois a manhã: o sexto dia.
pt.R: Deus olhou para tudo o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha feito, e tudo era muito bom. A tarde passou, e a manhã chegou. Esse foi o sexto dia.

am.L: እግዚአብሔርም የሠራውን ሁሉ አየ፤ እነሆም፣ እጅግ መልካም [ነበረ]። ምሽትም ሆነ፣ ጠዋትም ሆነ፤ ስድስተኛው ቀን።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር የሠራውን ሁሉ ተመለከተ፤ በእርግጥም እጅግ መልካም ነበር። ምሽት መጣ፣ ቀጥሎም ጠዋት መጣ፤ ይህ ስድስተኛው ቀን ነበር።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር የሠራውን ሁሉ ተመለከተ፤ ሁሉም በጣም ጥሩ ነበር። ምሽቱ አለፈ፤ ጠዋትም መጣ። ያ ስድስተኛው ቀን ነበር።

hi.L: और परमेश्वर ने वह सब देखा जो उन्होंने बनाया था, और देखो, [वह] बहुत अच्छा [था]। और शाम हुई और सुबह हुई, छठा दिन।
hi.B: परमेश्वर ने वह सब कुछ देखा जो उन्होंने बनाया था, और वह सचमुच बहुत ही अच्छा था। शाम हुई, फिर सुबह: छठा दिन।
hi.R: परमेश्वर ने वह सब कुछ देखा जो उन्होंने बनाया था, और वह बहुत अच्छा था। शाम ढली, और सुबह हुई। यह छठा दिन था।

ru.L: И Бог увидел всё, что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} создал, и вот, [это] очень хорошо. И настал вечер, и настало утро: день шестой.
ru.B: Бог посмотрел на всё, что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} создал, и это было поистине очень хорошо. Настал вечер, а потом утро: шестой день.
ru.R: Бог посмотрел на всё, что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} сделал, и это было очень хорошо. Прошёл вечер, и наступило утро. Это был шестой день.

uk.L: І побачив Бог усе, що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зробив, і ось, [усе було] дуже добре. І був вечір, і був ранок — день шостий.
uk.B: Бог подивився на все, що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зробив, і воно було справді дуже добре. Настав вечір, а потім ранок — шостий день.
uk.R: Бог подивився на все, що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зробив, і воно було дуже добре. Минув вечір, і настав ранок. Це був шостий день.

ja.L: そして神は、ご自分が造られたすべてのものを見られた。するとなんと、[それは]非常に良かった。そして夕べがあり、そして朝があった。その第六の日。
ja.B: 神はご自分が造られたすべてのものをご覧になった。それは実に、きわめて良かった。夕べが来て、それから朝が来た。六日目である。
ja.R: 神は、ご自分が造られたすべてのものをご覧になりました。それは、とても良いものでした。夕方が過ぎて、朝が来ました。これが六日目でした。

decisions.choice: and look, very good: the reader sees it with God
decisions.reason: The word "look" lets the reader see what God sees. This is the seventh time God sees that what he has made is good, and the only time the verdict is "very good": creation, with human beings in it, is complete and as it should be.

decisions.choice: the sixth day: the first of the days to have "the"
decisions.reason: Days two to five are "a second day", "a third day" and so on, without the article. The sixth day has it, as does the seventh (2:2-3), setting these days apart as the high point and the close of the week.

decisions.choice: a second day ... the sixth day (L); the second day ... the sixth day (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal follows the Hebrew: "a second day" and so on, then "the sixth day" (m2). Balanced and Readable say "the second day" and so on, as English counts.

decisions.choice: very good indeed
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "indeed" to give "very" the weight it has at the end of the verdicts (m1).

decisions.choice: y mira
decisions.reason: As in verse 29, "he aquí" is archaic. Literal keeps the word that invites the reader to look with God (m1), in the singular, since it is addressed to the reader, not to characters in the story; Balanced and Readable leave it unspoken.

decisions.choice: "ngày thứ sáu" at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives only the sixth day the article (m2). Vietnamese has no article, and "ấy" would point back to something already named, so the difference the English Literal shows is left to the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: "ስድስተኛው ቀን" with the definite ending at Literal, after "ሁለተኛ ቀን" ... "አምስተኛ ቀን" without it
decisions.reason: Amharic has no separate word for "the"; the ending -ው does its work. Literal adds it only on the sixth day, the first of the days to have the article in Hebrew (m2).

decisions.choice: "день шестой", as the earlier days
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives the sixth day the article, the first day to have one (m2). Russian has no article, so Literal cannot show it without adding words, and keeps the pattern of the other days.

decisions.choice: "するとなんと" for the Hebrew "look"; "その第六の日" with the article
decisions.reason: The word lets the reader see the result with God (m1); なんと carries that surprise in the narration without a command. その marks that this is the first day to have "the" (m2).
